const pool = H.pool('api-pool', [{ account, share: 1 }]);
const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet');

const scheduled = H.state('scheduled', 'pending');
const sampling = H.state('sampling', 'waiting');
const aWins = H.state('a-wins', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const experiment = H.kind('experiment')
  .data(z.object({ name: z.string() }))
  .states(scheduled, sampling, aWins, bWins, inconclusive);

const reading = z.object({ a: z.number(), b: z.number() });
const measure = H.command('measure-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ name: z.string() }))
  .output(reading)
  .argv(input => ['./experiments/measure', input.name])
  .on(local);
const judge = H.command('judge-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ name: z.string(), samples: z.array(reading) }))
  .output(z.object({ winner: z.enum(['a-wins', 'b-wins', 'inconclusive']) }))
  .argv(input => ['./experiments/judge', input.name, JSON.stringify(input.samples)])
  .on(local);

const runExperiment = H.flow('run-experiment').for(experiment).does(async ctx => {
  const startedMs = ctx.now().getTime();
  const samples: { a: number; b: number }[] = [];
  for (let hour = 1; hour <= 14 * 24; hour++) {
    const sample = await ctx.run(measure, { name: ctx.unit.data.name });
    if (sample.ok) samples.push(sample.value);
    await ctx.wait('sampling', { at: new Date(startedMs + hour * 3_600_000) });
  }
  const verdict = await ctx.run(judge, { name: ctx.unit.data.name, samples });
  return verdict.ok ? verdict.value.winner : ctx.fail(verdict.error);
});

const reviewDue = H.state('review-due', 'pending');
const betweenReviews = H.state('between-reviews', 'waiting');
const suspended = H.state('suspended', 'waiting');
const churned = H.state('churned', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const tenancy = H.kind('tenancy')
  .data(z.object({ customer: z.string(), nextReviewAt: z.string() }))
  .states(reviewDue, betweenReviews, suspended, churned);

const usageReport = H.command('usage-report')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['./tenancy/usage', input.customer])

  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), usage: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Summarize this month's usage for ${input.customer}:\n${input.usage}`);
const accountSummarizer = H.seat('account-summarizer', accountSummarizerRole).model(sonnet);
const upsell = H.halt('upsell', z.object({ upsell: z.boolean(), note: z.string() }))
  .about(z.object({ customer: z.string(), summary: z.string() }));

const monthlyReview = H.flow('monthly-review').for(tenancy).does(async ctx => {
  const customer = ctx.unit.data.customer;
  const usage = await ctx.run(usageReport, { customer });
  if (!usage.ok) return ctx.fail(usage.error);
  const summary = await ctx.run(accountSummarizer, { customer, usage: usage.value });
  if (!summary.ok) return ctx.fail(summary.error);
  await ctx.halt(upsell, `Upsell ${customer}?`, { customer, summary: summary.value.summary });
  await ctx.update({ nextReviewAt: new Date(ctx.now().getTime() + 30 * 86_400_000).toISOString() });
  return 'between-reviews';
});

const reviewClock = H.clock('tenancy-review-clock', tenancy, { daily: '04:00' }, tick =>
  tick.units

const ourTurn = H.state('our-turn', 'pending');
const theirTurn = H.state('their-turn', 'waiting');
const agreed = H.state('agreed', 'terminal', 'success');
const weWalkedAway = H.state('we-walked-away', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const theyWalkedAway = H.state('they-walked-away', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const expired = H.state('expired', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const negotiation = H.kind('negotiation')
  .data(z.object({
    vendor: z.string(),
    item: z.string(),
    expiresAt: z.string(),
    lastOffer: z.string().optional(),
    lastReply: z.string().optional(),
  }))
  .states(ourTurn, theirTurn, agreed, weWalkedAway, theyWalkedAway, expired);

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), lastOffer: z.string().optional(), lastReply: z.string().optional() }))
  .output(z.object({ action: z.enum(['offer', 'accept', 'walk-away']), offer: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Negotiate ${input.item} with ${input.vendor}. Our last offer: ${input.lastOffer ?? 'none'}. Their reply: ${input.lastReply ?? 'none'}.`);
const negotiator = H.seat('negotiator', negotiatorRole).model(sonnet);
const sendOffer = H.command('send-offer')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), offer: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['./procurement/send', input.vendor, input.offer])
  .on(local)
  .recovery('park');

const negotiationRound = H.flow('negotiation-round').for(negotiation).does(async ctx => {
  const next = await ctx.run(negotiator, ctx.unit.data);
  if (!next.ok) return ctx.fail(next.error);
  if (next.value.action === 'walk-away') return 'we-walked-away';
  const sent = await ctx.run(sendOffer, { vendor: ctx.unit.data.vendor, offer: next.value.offer });
  if (!sent.ok) return ctx.fail(sent.error);
  if (next.value.action === 'accept') return 'agreed';
  await ctx.update({ lastOffer: next.value.offer });
  return 'their-turn';
});

const vendorReplies = http.webhook(negotiation, {
  path: '/vendor-replies',
  secret: H.env('VENDOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
  body: z.object({ negotiation: z.string(), reply: z.string(), walkedAway: z.boolean() }),
  read: body => body.walkedAway
    ? { update: body.negotiation, state: 'they-walked-away' }
    : { update: body.negotiation, patch: { lastReply: body.reply }, state: 'our-turn' },
});

const experiments = H.lane('experiments', experiment)
  .handler(runExperiment)
  .suppliers(H.operator)
  .store(sqlite.store(experiment, './.harness/units.db'));
const tenancies = H.lane('tenancies', tenancy)
  .handler(monthlyReview)
  .suppliers(H.operator, reviewClock)
  .store(sqlite.store(tenancy, './.harness/units.db'))
  .wip(4);
const negotiations = H.lane('negotiations', negotiation)
  .handler(negotiationRound)
  .suppliers(H.operator, vendorReplies)
  .store(sqlite.store(negotiation, './.harness/units.db'))
  .wip(2);

const negotiationExpiry = H.trigger(
  'negotiation-expiry',
  H.on.deadline(negotiation, data => new Date(data.expiresAt), ['our-turn', 'their-turn']),
  (event, act) => act.move('expired'),
);

const inconclusiveShare = (metrics: Metrics) => metrics.rate({
  among: { entry: 'transition', kind: experiment, position: 'terminal' },
  count: { entry: 'transition', kind: experiment, state: 'inconclusive' },
  days: 180,
});
const lifecycles = H.policy.scheduler('lifecycles', view => {
  const share = inconclusiveShare(view.metrics);
  const holdExperiments = share.samples >= 10 && share.value !== null && share.value > 0.5;
  return { start: view.pending.filter(unit => !(holdExperiments && unit.is(experiment))) };
});

export const harness = H.harness('lifecycles')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('./.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(experiments, tenancies, negotiations)
  .pools(pool)
  .triggers(negotiationExpiry)
  .scheduler(lifecycles)
  .clients(claude.supervisor({ grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readTelemetry] }))
  .observers(markdown.board('./BOARD.md'));

# ours-2, merged: facets fold into resources

This child of g00-ours-2-1 applies the **merge** operator once. The facet and the resource are made one entity. It also repairs the adversary's three sharpest critiques and the scenario-7 defect.

## The merge: `Facet` + `Resource` → `Resource`

### Why they rhyme

The parent had two vocabulary entities that do the same job: each is a named thing that other entities reference by identity.

- **Resource** (principle 8): "a named shared thing that leases, memory scope and metric facets reference by identity."
- **Facet** (principle 18): "a declared dimension that is not a column."

In practice, every use of a facet in the battery is one of three things:

- a memory scope (scenarios 6 and 9);
- a metric dimension (scenarios 2, 9 and 11);
- a unit tag (scenarios 6, 9 and 11).

The resource already served memory scope and metric dimensions. The only difference was that a facet has many values, while the parent's resource was a single thing. Scenario 12 then faked the many-valued case for resources, with a `databases` record of two resources.

### The merged entity

`H.resource(n)` is now the one noun.

- A resource used whole is a single shared thing, such as `app-code`.
- `resource.is(value)` names one member of it, such as `database.is('orders')` or `category.is('billing')`. It produces a `ResourceValue`.
- Leases, memory scope (`when.resources`), metric dimensions (`.by(category)`), unit tags (`flow.tag(category, …)`) and creation values (`lane.create(child, e => [category.is(…)])`) all accept either form.

### What it buys

- **Principle 14 is repaired.** The envelope's `when` is back to exactly kinds, roles, skills and resources. The parent's knowing bend (a fifth `facets` slot) is gone.
- **Scenario 12 gets real per-database locks.** `database.is(input.database).exclusive()` replaces the hand-built record of resources.
- **One fewer entity and one fewer `H.*` method.**

### What it costs (honesty)

1. **A category is not shared.** A support category is not a "shared thing" in the plain sense of principle 8. Nothing stops an author writing `category.is('billing').exclusive()`, and the kernel will honour it by serialising billing work. That is meaningful but rarely intended. The type system cannot tell a lockable resource from a classifying one, because they are now one type.
2. **Values are open-ended.** Members of a resource are runtime strings, not declared entities. `category.is(s.classify.category)` mints a member from model output. Principle 8's "a string never stands in for it" now holds for the resource itself, but not for its members. Members are data under a declared entity. That is how a data value can be a dimension without declaring every category ahead of time.
3. **Weakness 4 grows.** The resource-binding plugin (the file-lease guard's `area`) maps whole resources. A family resource leased by member, such as `database`, needs no binding, because the lease table keys on `resource:value`. The startup check therefore applies only to whole resources claimed by an agent's file tools.

## Entities

### Kinds (vocabulary, no backend)

- **`H.work`**: the kind of a unit, its schema and its states.
- **`H.state`**: shareable. Each declares its position. A terminal state declares its verdict.
- **`H.resource`**: a whole resource or, through `.is(v)`, a member.
- **`H.halt`**: a named question with a context and a decision schema.
- **`H.memory`**: a memory kind.
- **`H.role`**: a role.
- **`H.skill`**: the typed contract for one model call.

### Instances (carry a backend)

- **Account.** `H.account(n, driver).quota(partition)`. The account no longer carries a share.
- **Model.** `H.model(id, opts).pricing(p)`.
- **Command.** `H.command(…)`.
- **Job.** `H.job(…)`, as a general external job or `.batch(seat)`.
- **Runners** live in `harness-dsl/runners`.

### Pivots

- **Seat.** Role × skill × models × choice policy.
- **Pool.** Accounts × shares × policy, written `H.pool(n, accounts).share(account, ratio).serves(...).policy(p).fallback(a)`.
- **Lane.** Work kind × suppliers × store × handler.
- **Journal.** Memory kind × store × recall.
- **Grant.** Client × operations.

### Execution

Unchanged from the parent, apart from the items listed under *What changed and why*: flow, trigger, streams, metric, policy and consequences.

## Rules

Only the rules that changed or matter here are repeated. Everything else is as in the parent.

### Moving and cancelling units

There are two verbs: `lane.move(select, to)` and `lane.cancel(select, to)`.

- **`move`** never ends an attempt.
  - On a unit with no live attempt, it applies at once.
  - On a unit whose attempt is running, blocked or suspended, it is recorded and applied when the attempt next ends. It is the same deferral rule as supplier updates.
- **`cancel`** ends the unit's live attempt with outcome `cancelled`, then moves the unit with cause `cancelled`.
  - On a unit with no live attempt, it is a move.
  - A cancellation is never counted against a model, seat, runner or account.
- **Selectors** are unchanged. `{ halted, key }` selects units whose attempt is blocked at that halt, so `cancel({ halted: replyApproval, key }, fresh)` cancels a draft awaiting approval and nothing else.
- **Reopen, wake and re-entry** are all `move`. Only `cancel` destroys work, and its name says so.

### Retry exhaustion must have a way out

`retry.exhausted` stays required, as principles 12 and 11 require.

- The target must be either a terminal state, or a waiting state that something can leave.
- A waiting state can be left when it is the `from` of a registered move or cancel selector, or the `failed` target of an `.order`.
- Any other target is a startup error, with this message: *"exhaustion target `stalled` of lane `x` has no exit; use a terminal state"*.
- Dead-end waiting states are therefore unwritable. A kind that wants "gave up" declares a terminal state such as `abandoned`, with its own verdict, usually failure.

### Ordering holds

`.order({ after, failed })` works as follows.

- A unit whose predecessor ends with a failure verdict moves to `failed` (cause `order`, with the reason recorded) and is *held*.
- If the predecessor later reaches a success verdict (an operator retries it), the held unit is released back to its pending state (cause `released`).
- The board lists held units with their reason and with the key that would release them. "Nothing will happen" and "someone outside will reply" are therefore distinguishable.

### Ceiling decisions are kernel-owned

`.ceiling({ maxUsd, halt, context, stopped })` halts the attempt before a step that would pass `maxUsd`.

- The halt's decision type must extend `CeilingDecision = { raiseToUsd?: number }`. This is checked at compile time.
- If the decision raises the ceiling above the amount already spent, the attempt continues under the new ceiling.
- Any other decision ends the attempt `cancelled`, and the unit moves to `stopped` (cause `ceiling`).
- The meaning of the decision no longer depends on a schema the author happened to write.

### Metrics read by entity, never by string

- `metrics.read(metric, ...at)` takes **entities** as key values.
  - A column value is the entity of that column: a `Model`, a seat, a lane, a work kind, a state, an account, a halt or a job. The resolver column takes `'human' | 'policy' | 'clock'`.
  - A resource dimension takes a `ResourceValue` of that resource.
- The allowed value types are computed from the metric's `by(...)` dimensions. `read(approvals, category.is(c), sonnet)` type-checks, and `read(approvals, region.is(r))` does not.
- Renaming a resource renames every key with it.
- Crossing events expose `event.of(category)`. This is restricted to the resource dimensions of the crossed metric.

### Seat credit

`stream.credit(...seats)` emits one record per listed seat per event.

- The **seat column** is set to that seat.
- The **model column** is set to the model that seat ran on in the same attempt. This is read from the ledger's invocation records for that attempt. If the seat was not invoked in that attempt, no record is emitted for it.
- An owner-defined A/B metric therefore keys on the seat, and may also key on the model. For example: `H.events.decisions(editorial).credit(reviewerA, reviewerB).rate(c => actedOn(c.event).includes(c.seat))`.
- Swapping a seat's model keeps the seat series.
- The decision schema no longer has to mirror the parallel-call keys.

### Shared accounts, per-harness shares

- An account is one descriptor, imported by both harnesses of scenario 7. It names its quota partition.
- The share cap is a relationship between this harness and that account, so it lives on the pool (`pool.share(account, 0.6)`). No derived account descriptors exist, so principle 11's one-name rule holds.
- `AccountCandidate.maxQuotaShare` is computed from the pool. The folded `QuotaState.byHarness` shows each harness's consumption of the shared window.
- A client may name a `session` (an adapter option). Two clients with one session are one supervisor session holding two endpoints. The `Client.session` field lets the adapter join them.

### Startup validation (additions)

`start()` now also fails on:

- an exhaustion target with no exit;
- a pool `share` for an account not in the pool;
- a `ceiling.stopped` target that is not terminal;
- two resources with one name, which covers what was a facet-versus-resource clash;
- a resource name that repeats a column name.

## What changed and why

Changes are listed against the parent, g00-ours-2-1.

1. **Facet merged into resource** (operator). `H.facet`, `Facet`, `FacetValue`, `DimName` and `ScopeInput.facets` are removed. `Resource.is(value)` gives a `ResourceValue`.
   - The kernel's `Scope.resources` is now `{ resource, value? }[]`.
   - `UnitMeta.facets` becomes `resources`, and `NewRecord.facets` becomes `values`.
   - The honesty cost is listed above.
2. **`lane.cancel` split from `lane.move`** (critique c). `move` never kills an attempt and defers while one is live. Scenario 2's reply-while-classifying no longer kills classify. The deferred update fires once the attempt blocks at approval, and `cancel({ halted })` acts then.
3. **Ceiling decision has kernel meaning** (critique c). `CeilingDecision` is kernel-owned, and the lane declares a terminal `stopped` state.
4. **Exhaustion targets must have an exit** (critique a). Dead-end waiting states become a startup error. Order-parked units are held with a release, and the board shows `held`.
5. **Metric keys are entities** (critique b). `MetricsReader.read(metric, ...DimValue<Key>[])` replaces the string-keyed record. `CrossingEvent.of(resource)` replaces `e.key.category`.
6. **`stream.credit(...seats)`** (critique b, scenario 6). Owner-defined A/B metrics key on the seat, as principle 8's seat ruling requires.
7. **Shares moved from account to pool** (scenario 7 critique, weakness 5 in part). The account is an instance with a backend; the share is a per-harness relationship, and so it lives on a pivot.
8. **Client `session`** (weakness 8, scenario 7). One supervisor session can hold endpoints into several harnesses.
9. **`ModelChoice.seat` and `RecallChoice.seat`** are now seat entities, not names.
10. **`TransitionEvent.reason`** carries the order or ceiling reason, so a parked 0042 says why on the board and in metrics.
11. **Credit sets the model column too** (scenarios 2 and 3, written against this surface). Two scenarios need a model dimension on owner-defined metrics:
    - Scenario 3's synthesizer A/B ranks two models by citation-check pass rate, but the citation check is a command with no model of its own.
    - Scenario 2's approval rate "by model" is read from halt decisions, whose own model field belongs to the resolver.

    With `credit(seat)`, the credited record carries the seat's model from the same attempt, so `.by('model')` means the model that did the work being judged. There is no new method or type; the rule is now stated where it was silent.

### Defects not taken up

These are listed openly rather than repaired:

- **Jurisdictional quorum** (the adversary's scenario 13): resolvers scoped by lane, and multi-person approval, are not in the battery. A grant still names a halt without a lane scope. The repair would be `H.ops.resolve(halt).in(lane)`, but no battery scenario calls it, so principle 21 keeps it out.
- **Lane breadth** (weakness 6) is unchanged.
- **A decision inside a `when` branch is dropped from the flow state.** A halt's decision taken inside `when` is recorded on the ledger, but it does not reach later steps, because `when` returns its input state type.
  - Scenario 1's owner call is therefore not passed back to the builder in the same round.
  - Scenarios 2–6, written against this surface, do not depend on it.
  - The repair would be an optional merge of the branch state, and it is left for a later generation.

## Principles broken

None.

- The parent's bend of 14 is repaired by the merge: memory scope uses resources only.
- The cost of the merge, a category being a resource it is odd to lease, sits within principle 8's text. Principle 8 lists memory scope and metric facets among what references a resource.

import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';
import { plugins } from 'harness-dsl/plugins';

const queued = H.state('queued').pending();
const done = H.state('done').terminal('success');
const abandoned = H.state('abandoned').terminal('failure');
const due = H.state('due').pending();
const healthy = H.state('healthy').terminal('success');
const unhealthy = H.state('unhealthy').terminal('failure');

const ticketSchema = z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string(), reporter: z.string() });
const epicSchema = z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() });
const serviceSchema = z.object({ service: z.string(), url: z.string() });

const epic = H.work('Epic').schema(epicSchema).states(queued, done, abandoned);
const feature = H.work('Feature').schema(ticketSchema).states(queued, done, abandoned);
const bug = H.work('Bug').schema(ticketSchema).states(queued, done, abandoned);
const heartbeat = H.work('ServiceHeartbeat').schema(serviceSchema).states(due, healthy, unhealthy);

const appCode = H.resource('app-code');

const experience = H.memory('experience').content(z.object({ rule: z.string() })).trust('experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste').content(z.object({ rule: z.string() })).trust('taste');

const lessons = H.journal('lessons').of(experience).store(jsonl.memory('.harness/experience.jsonl')).recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 8 }));
const preferences = H.journal('preferences').of(taste).store(jsonl.memory('.harness/taste.jsonl')).recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 12 }));

const quota = sqlite.quota('.harness/quota.db');
const max1 = H.account('max-1', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_1_DIR') })).quota(quota);
const max2 = H.account('max-2', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_2_DIR') })).quota(quota);
const max3 = H.account('max-3', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_3_DIR') })).quota(quota);
const api = H.account('api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') })).quota(quota);

const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5', { budgetTokens: 32000 }).pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const opus = H.model('claude-opus-4-1', { budgetTokens: 32000 }).pricing(anthropic.pricing());

const claude = H.pool('claude', [max1, max2, max3, api])
  .share(max1, 0.8)
  .share(max2, 0.8)
  .share(max3, 0.5)
  .serves(sonnet, opus)
  .policy(policies.soonestReset())
  .fallback(api);

const bugs = H.lane('bugs').of(bug);
const features = H.lane('features').of(feature);
const epics = H.lane('epics').of(epic);
const heartbeats = H.lane('heartbeats').of(heartbeat);

const bugSuccess = H.metric('bug-success-by-model', H.events.transitions(bugs, { terminal: true }))
  .rate(e => e.verdict === 'success')
  .by('model')
  .window('14d');
const featureSuccess = H.metric('feature-success-by-model', H.events.transitions(features, { terminal: true }))
  .rate(e => e.verdict === 'success')
  .by('model')
  .window('14d');

const cheaperUntilSlip = H.policy.models('cheaper-until-slip', c => {
  const outcomes = c.unit.lane === features.name ? featureSuccess : bugSuccess;
  const cheap = c.metrics.read(outcomes, sonnet);
  const slipped = cheap.samples >= 20 && (cheap.value ?? 1) < 0.85;
  return slipped ? [opus, sonnet] : [sonnet, opus];
});

const local = runners.local({ name: 'local', slots: 4 });

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks')
  .input(z.object({ workspace: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ ok: z.boolean(), report: z.string() }))
  .runner(local)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.exec(['npm', 'run', 'check'], { cwd: input.workspace });
    return { ok: result.code === 0, report: result.stdout + result.stderr };
  });

const probe = H.command('probe-service')
  .input(serviceSchema)
  .output(z.object({ healthy: z.boolean(), status: z.number() }))
  .runner(local)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async input => {
    const response = await fetch(input.url);
    return { healthy: response.ok, status: response.status };
  });

const ownerCall = H.halt('owner-call')
  .context(z.object({ question: z.string() }))
  .decision(z.object({ answer: z.string() }))
  .ask(c => c.question);

const buildChange = H.skill('build-change')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string(), round: z.number() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), question: z.string().optional() }))
  .prompt(i => `Round ${i.round}. Implement: ${i.title}\n\n${i.body}`);

const auditChange = H.skill('audit-change')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), summary: z.string(), round: z.number() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(i => `Audit round ${i.round} of "${i.title}". Builder summary:\n${i.summary}\nList every deficit that remains.`);

const planEpic = H.skill('plan-epic')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ key: z.string(), title: z.string(), body: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt(i => `Decompose the epic "${i.title}" into features.\n\n${i.body}`);

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .promptFile('prompts/builder.md')
  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience, taste)
  .use(plugins.fileLeaseGuard().area(appCode, ['src/**', 'tests/**']), plugins.stopCheck(projectChecks));
const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .promptFile('prompts/auditor.md')
  .intents(['read', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience)
  .record(experience);
const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .promptFile('prompts/planner.md')
  .intents(['read'])
  .recall(taste);

const builder = H.seat('builder').role(builderRole).skill(buildChange).models(sonnet, opus).policy(cheaperUntilSlip);
const auditor = H.seat('auditor').role(auditorRole).skill(auditChange).models(opus);
const planner = H.seat('planner').role(plannerRole).skill(planEpic).models(opus);

const ticketFlow = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string(), rounds: z.number() }))
  .use(plugins.gitWorktree({ base: 'main' }))
  .loop('round', {
    max: s => s.input.rounds,
    body: f => f
      .step('build', builder, s => ({ title: s.input.title, body: s.input.body, round: s.round.iteration }))
      .when(s => s.build.question !== undefined, g => g.halt('ownerCall', ownerCall, s => ({ question: s.build.question ?? '' })))
      .step('audit', auditor, s => ({ title: s.input.title, summary: s.build.summary, round: s.round.iteration })),
    until: s => s.audit.deficits.length === 0,
  })
  .when(s => s.audit.deficits.length === 0, f => f.exit('done'))
  .exit('roundsOut');

const epicFlow = H.flow('decompose-epic')
  .input(epicSchema)
  .step('plan', planner, s => ({ title: s.input.title, body: s.input.body }))
  .spawn('features', features, s => s.plan.features.map(f => ({ key: f.key, data: { title: f.title, body: f.body, reporter: 'epic' } })))
  .when(s => s.features.every(child => child.verdict === 'success'), f => f.exit('delivered'))
  .exit('incomplete');

const heartbeatFlow = H.flow('heartbeat')
  .input(serviceSchema)
  .step('probe', probe, s => s.input)
  .when(s => !s.probe.healthy, f => f.exit('unhealthy'))
  .exit('healthy');

const trackerStates = { [queued.name]: 'Todo', [done.name]: 'Done', [abandoned.name]: 'Canceled' };
const linearKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const ticketStore = linear.store({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'PRD', schema: ticketSchema, states: trackerStates });
const epicStore = linear.store({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'PRD', schema: epicSchema, states: trackerStates });

const bugLane = bugs
  .from(
    linear.issues({ name: 'linear-bugs', apiKey: linearKey, team: 'PRD', labels: ['bug'], data: i => ({ title: i.title, body: i.description, reporter: 'linear' }) }),
    folder.files({ name: 'bug-folder', path: 'bugs', glob: '*.md', data: file => ({ title: file.name, body: file.body, reporter: 'folder' }) }),
    manual('operator-bugs'),
  )
  .store(ticketStore)
  .handle(ticketFlow, {
    input: u => ({ title: u.data.title, body: u.data.body, rounds: 3 }),
    exits: { done, roundsOut: { to: queued, atMost: 1, then: abandoned } },
    retry: { retries: 2, backoff: { initial: '2m', factor: 2 }, exhausted: abandoned },
  })
  .wip(2);

const featureLane = features
  .from(
    linear.issues({ name: 'linear-features', apiKey: linearKey, team: 'PRD', labels: ['feature'], data: i => ({ title: i.title, body: i.description, reporter: 'linear' }) }),
    manual('operator-features'),
  )
  .store(ticketStore)
  .handle(ticketFlow, {
    input: u => ({ title: u.data.title, body: u.data.body, rounds: 5 }),
    exits: { done, roundsOut: { to: queued, atMost: 1, then: abandoned } },
    retry: { retries: 2, backoff: { initial: '2m', factor: 2 }, exhausted: abandoned },
  });

const epicLane = epics
  .from(linear.issues({ name: 'linear-epics', apiKey: linearKey, team: 'PRD', labels: ['epic'], data: i => ({ title: i.title, body: i.description }) }))
  .store(epicStore)
  .handle(epicFlow, {
    exits: { delivered: done, incomplete: { to: queued, atMost: 2, then: abandoned } },
    retry: { retries: 1, backoff: { initial: '10m', factor: 2 }, exhausted: abandoned },
  })
  .wip(1);

const heartbeatLane = heartbeats
  .from(schedule.cron({
    name: 'heartbeat-every-5m',
    cron: '*/5 * * * *',
    children: at => [{ key: `api-${at.toISOString()}`, data: { service: 'api', url: 'https://api.example.com/health' } }],
  }))
  .handle(heartbeatFlow, {
    exits: { healthy, unhealthy },
    retry: { retries: 0, backoff: 'none', exhausted: unhealthy },
  });

const heartbeatFailureFilesBug = H.trigger('heartbeat-failure-files-bug')
  .on(H.events.transitions(heartbeats, { to: unhealthy }))
  .do(bugs.create(e => ({
    key: `heartbeat-${e.unit.key}`,
    data: { title: `Service ${e.unit.data.service} failed its heartbeat`, body: `Probe of ${e.unit.data.url} failed at ${e.at.toISOString()}.`, reporter: 'heartbeat' },
  })));

const laneOrder: readonly string[] = [heartbeats.name, bugs.name, features.name, epics.name];
const featureStarvedAfterMs = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const rank = (candidate: Candidate, now: Date): number =>
  candidate.lane === features.name && now.getTime() - candidate.queuedAt.getTime() > featureStarvedAfterMs
    ? 0.5
    : laneOrder.indexOf(candidate.lane);

const priority = H.policy.units('heartbeats-bugs-features-epics', c =>
  [...c.candidates].sort((a, b) => rank(a, c.now) - rank(b, c.now) || a.queuedAt.getTime() - b.queuedAt.getTime()));

const supervisor = H.grant(
  claudeCode.client({ name: 'supervisor' }),
  H.ops.work.read,
  H.ops.work.write,
  H.ops.resolve(ownerCall),
  H.ops.attempts.manage,
  H.ops.memory.write(experience),
  H.ops.memory.write(taste),
  H.ops.telemetry.read,
  H.ops.accounts.manage,
  H.operation('probe-production', probe),
);

export const codingTeam = H.harness('coding-team')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .pools(claude)
  .lanes(heartbeatLane, bugLane, featureLane, epicLane)
  .journals(lessons, preferences)
  .triggers(heartbeatFailureFilesBug)
  .scheduler(priority)
  .grants(supervisor)
  .observe(observers.board({ path: 'BOARD.md' }), observers.telemetry({ path: 'TELEMETRY.md' }));

void codingTeam.start();

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { Candidate } from 'harness-dsl/kernel';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { http } from 'harness-dsl/http';
import { rest } from 'harness-dsl/rest';
import { runners } from 'harness-dsl/runners';
import { policies } from 'harness-dsl/policies';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';

const fresh = H.state('new').pending();
const replied = H.state('sent').waiting();
const closedByCustomer = H.state('closed-by-customer').terminal('success');
const escalated = H.state('escalated').terminal('failure');
const opened = H.state('opened').pending();
const handled = H.state('handled').terminal('success');
const unhandled = H.state('unhandled').terminal('failure');

const conversationSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  customer: z.string(),
  subject: z.string(),
  lastMessage: z.string(),
  lastMessageId: z.string(),
  status: z.enum(['open', 'closed']),
  slaDue: z.string(),
});
const escalationSchema = z.object({ conversationId: z.string(), customer: z.string(), reason: z.string() });

const conversation = H.work('Conversation').schema(conversationSchema).states(fresh, replied, closedByCustomer, escalated);
const escalation = H.work('Escalation').schema(escalationSchema).states(opened, handled, unhandled);

const category = H.resource('category');

const taste = H.memory('reply-taste').content(z.object({ rule: z.string() })).trust('taste').curated();
const experience = H.memory('support-experience').content(z.object({ rule: z.string() })).trust('experience');
const tasteJournal = H.journal('reply-taste').of(taste).store(jsonl.memory('.harness/taste.jsonl')).recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 10 }));
const experienceJournal = H.journal('support-experience').of(experience).store(jsonl.memory('.harness/experience.jsonl')).recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 8 }));

const api = H.account('api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') })).quota(sqlite.quota('.harness/quota.db'));
const haiku = H.model('claude-haiku-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const pool = H.pool('anthropic', [api]).share(api, 1).serves(haiku, sonnet);

const classifyMessage = H.skill('classify-message')
  .input(z.object({ subject: z.string(), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ category: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Subject: ${i.subject}\n\n${i.message}\n\nName the support category.`);
const draftReply = H.skill('draft-reply')
  .input(z.object({ category: z.string(), customer: z.string(), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ reply: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Draft a reply to ${i.customer} about a ${i.category} question:\n\n${i.message}`);

const classifierRole = H.role('classifier').prompt('You sort support conversations into exactly one category.');
const drafterRole = H.role('drafter').prompt('You draft replies a human will approve before sending.').recall(taste, experience);

const classifier = H.seat('classifier').role(classifierRole).skill(classifyMessage).models(haiku);
const drafter = H.seat('drafter').role(drafterRole).skill(draftReply).models(sonnet);

const replyApproval = H.halt('reply-approval')
  .context(z.object({ category: z.string(), draft: z.string() }))
  .decision(z.object({ approved: z.boolean(), edited: z.string().optional() }))
  .ask(c => `Approve this ${c.category} reply?\n\n${c.draft}`);
const costCeiling = H.halt('conversation-cost-ceiling')
  .context(z.object({ spentUsd: z.number(), nextStep: z.string() }))
  .decision(z.object({ raiseToUsd: z.number().optional() }))
  .ask(c => `This conversation has spent $${c.spentUsd.toFixed(2)}; ${c.nextStep} would pass $0.40.`);
const escalationHandled = H.halt('escalation-handled')
  .context(z.object({ conversationId: z.string(), reason: z.string() }))
  .decision(z.object({ resolution: z.string() }))
  .ask(c => `Escalated conversation ${c.conversationId}: ${c.reason}`);

const approvals = H.metric('approval-rate', H.events.decisions(replyApproval).where(d => d.resolver === 'human').credit(drafter))
  .rate(c => c.event.decision.approved)
  .by(category, 'model')
  .window('90d');

const safeCategory = H.policy.decision('safe-category', replyApproval, c => {
  const record = c.metrics.read(approvals, category.is(c.context.category));
  return record.samples >= 200 && record.value === 1 ? { approved: true } : undefined;
});

const helpdeskUrl = H.env('HELPDESK_URL');
const helpdeskToken = H.env('HELPDESK_TOKEN');
const helpdeskRunner = runners.local({ name: 'helpdesk', slots: 4 }).env({ HELPDESK_URL: helpdeskUrl, HELPDESK_TOKEN: helpdeskToken });

const sendReply = H.command('send-reply')
  .input(z.object({ conversationId: z.string(), body: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ messageId: z.string() }))
  .runner(helpdeskRunner)
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.exec(['./bin/helpdesk-reply', input.conversationId], { stdin: input.body });
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
    return { messageId: result.stdout.trim() };
  });
const postNote = H.command('post-escalation-note')
  .input(z.object({ conversationId: z.string(), note: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ posted: z.boolean() }))
  .runner(helpdeskRunner)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.exec(['./bin/helpdesk-note', input.conversationId], { stdin: input.note });
    return { posted: result.code === 0 };
  });

const replyFlow = H.flow('reply')
  .input(conversationSchema)
  .step('classify', classifier, s => ({ subject: s.input.subject, message: s.input.lastMessage }))
  .tag(category, s => s.classify.category)
  .step('draft', drafter, s => ({ category: s.classify.category, customer: s.input.customer, message: s.input.lastMessage }))
  .halt('approval', replyApproval, s => ({ category: s.classify.category, draft: s.draft.reply }), { resolver: safeCategory })
  .when(s => !s.approval.approved, f => f.exit('rejected'))
  .step('send', sendReply, s => ({ conversationId: s.input.id, body: s.approval.edited ?? s.draft.reply }))
  .exit('sent');

const escalationFlow = H.flow('escalation')
  .input(escalationSchema)
  .halt('handled', escalationHandled, s => ({ conversationId: s.input.conversationId, reason: s.input.reason }))
  .step('note', postNote, s => ({ conversationId: s.input.conversationId, note: s.handled.resolution }))
  .exit('handled');

const conversations = H.lane('conversations').of(conversation);
const escalations = H.lane('escalations').of(escalation);

const conversationLane = conversations
  .from(
    http.webhook({
      name: 'helpdesk-webhook',
      path: '/helpdesk',
      port: H.slot.port(0),
      secret: H.env('HELPDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
      body: z.object({ conversation: conversationSchema }),
      key: b => b.conversation.id,
      data: b => b.conversation,
      mode: 'upsert',
    }),
    rest.poll({
      name: 'helpdesk-sweep',
      baseUrl: helpdeskUrl,
      token: helpdeskToken,
      path: '/conversations?status=open',
      interval: '10m',
      item: conversationSchema,
      key: c => c.id,
      data: c => c,
      mode: 'upsert',
    }),
  )
  .store(rest.store({ name: 'helpdesk', baseUrl: helpdeskUrl, token: helpdeskToken, path: '/conversations', schema: conversationSchema }))
  .handle(replyFlow, {
    exits: { sent: replied, rejected: { to: fresh, atMost: 2, then: escalated } },
    retry: { retries: 2, backoff: { initial: '30s', factor: 2 }, exhausted: escalated },
  })
  .ceiling({
    maxUsd: 0.4,
    halt: costCeiling,
    context: c => ({ spentUsd: c.spentUsd, nextStep: c.nextStep }),
    stopped: escalated,
  });

const escalationLane = escalations.handle(escalationFlow, {
  exits: { handled },
  retry: { retries: 1, backoff: 'none', exhausted: unhandled },
});

const slaBreach = H.trigger('sla-breach')
  .on(H.time.at(conversations, d => (d.status === 'open' ? new Date(d.slaDue) : undefined)))
  .do(
    escalations.create(e => ({
      key: `escalation-${e.unit.key}`,
      data: { conversationId: e.unit.data.id, customer: e.unit.data.customer, reason: `SLA breached at ${e.deadline.toISOString()}` },
    })),
    conversations.cancel(e => e.unit.key, escalated),
  );

const customerReplied = H.trigger('customer-replied')
  .on(H.events.updates(conversations).where(u => u.unit.data.lastMessageId !== u.previous.lastMessageId && u.unit.data.status === 'open'))
  .do(
    conversations.cancel({ halted: replyApproval, key: u => u.unit.key }, fresh),
    conversations.move(u => u.unit.key, fresh),
  );

const customerClosed = H.trigger('customer-closed')
  .on(H.events.updates(conversations).where(u => u.unit.data.status === 'closed' && u.previous.status === 'open'))
  .do(conversations.cancel(u => u.unit.key, closedByCustomer));

const reviewerEdits = H.trigger('reviewer-edits-become-taste')
  .on(H.events.decisions(replyApproval).where(d => d.resolver === 'human' && d.decision.edited !== undefined))
  .do(tasteJournal.record(d => ({
    content: { rule: `When replying about ${d.context.category}, write it the way the reviewer did: "${d.decision.edited ?? ''}", because the reviewer rewrote "${d.context.draft}".` },
    when: { roles: [drafterRole], resources: [category.is(d.context.category)] },
  })));

const urgency = (candidate: Candidate): number =>
  conversations.holds(candidate) ? Date.parse(candidate.data.slaDue) : 0;
const timeToBreach = H.policy.units('time-to-breach', c => [...c.candidates].sort((a, b) => urgency(a) - urgency(b)));

const reviewer = H.grant(
  claudeCode.client({ name: 'reviewer' }),
  H.ops.work.read,
  H.ops.work.write,
  H.ops.resolve(replyApproval),
  H.ops.resolve(costCeiling),
  H.ops.resolve(escalationHandled),
  H.ops.memory.write(taste),
  H.ops.memory.curate(taste),
  H.ops.memory.write(experience),
  H.ops.telemetry.read,
);

export const supportTriage = H.harness('support-triage')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .pools(pool)
  .lanes(conversationLane, escalationLane)
  .journals(tasteJournal, experienceJournal)
  .triggers(slaBreach, customerReplied, customerClosed, reviewerEdits)
  .scheduler(timeToBreach)
  .grants(reviewer)
  .observe(observers.board({ path: 'BOARD.md' }), observers.telemetry({ path: 'TELEMETRY.md' }));

void supportTriage.start();

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { http } from 'harness-dsl/http';
import { manual } from 'harness-dsl/supply';
import { policies } from 'harness-dsl/policies';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';

const store = './.harness/units.sqlite';
const api = H.account('anthropic-api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }));
const haiku = H.model('claude-haiku-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());

const experimentSchema = z.object({ name: z.string(), metricQuery: z.string() });
const scheduledExperiment = H.state('scheduled').pending();
const aWins = H.state('a-wins').terminal('neutral');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins').terminal('neutral');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive').terminal('neutral');
const experimentAbandoned = H.state('experiment-abandoned').terminal('failure');
const experiment = H.work('Experiment').schema(experimentSchema).states(scheduledExperiment, aWins, bWins, inconclusive, experimentAbandoned);

const measurement = z.object({ status: z.enum(['running', 'A', 'B', 'inconclusive']), samples: z.number() });

const twoWeekRun = H.job('two-week-run')
  .input(z.object({ name: z.string(), metricQuery: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ winner: z.enum(['A', 'B', 'inconclusive']), samples: z.number() }))
  .submit(async (input, ctx) => {
    const started = await ctx.exec(['experiments', 'start', input.name, '--duration', '14d', '--metric', input.metricQuery]);
    return started.stdout.trim();
  })
  .collect(async (ref, ctx) => {
    const measured = await ctx.exec(['experiments', 'measure', ref, '--json']);
    if (measured.code !== 0) return { status: 'failed', reason: measured.stderr };
    const m = measurement.parse(JSON.parse(measured.stdout));
    if (m.status === 'running') return { status: 'pending' };
    return { status: 'done', output: { winner: m.status, samples: m.samples } };
  })
  .every('1h');

const experimentFlow = H.flow('experiment')
  .input(experimentSchema)
  .step('run', twoWeekRun, s => ({ name: s.input.name, metricQuery: s.input.metricQuery }))
  .when(s => s.run.winner === 'A', f => f.exit('aWins'))
  .when(s => s.run.winner === 'B', f => f.exit('bWins'))
  .exit('inconclusive');

const experiments = H.lane('experiments')
  .of(experiment)
  .from(manual('operator-experiments'))
  .store(sqlite.store(store))
  .handle(experimentFlow, {
    exits: { aWins, bWins, inconclusive },
    retry: { retries: 1, backoff: { initial: '1h', factor: 2 }, exhausted: experimentAbandoned },
  });

const inconclusiveShare = H.metric('experiments-inconclusive', H.events.transitions(experiments, { terminal: true }))
  .rate(e => e.to === inconclusive.name)
  .window('365d');

const tenancySchema = z.object({
  customer: z.string(),
  plan: z.string(),
  billing: z.enum(['paid', 'overdue']),
  churned: z.boolean(),
});
const reviewDue = H.state('review-due').pending();
const current = H.state('current').waiting();
const suspended = H.state('suspended').waiting();
const reviewFailed = H.state('review-failed').waiting();
const churned = H.state('churned').terminal('neutral');
const tenancy = H.work('Tenancy').schema(tenancySchema).states(reviewDue, current, suspended, reviewFailed, churned);

const usageReview = H.command('usage-review')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ usage: z.string() }))
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const report = await ctx.exec(['billing', 'usage', input.customer, '--last', '30d']);
    return { usage: report.stdout };
  });
const accountManager = H.role('account-manager').promptFile('./prompts/account-manager.md');
const summarizeTenancy = H.skill('summarize-tenancy')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), plan: z.string(), usage: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Customer ${i.customer} on ${i.plan}. Usage:\n${i.usage}\nSummarize for an upsell decision.`);
const tenancySummarizer = H.seat('tenancy-summarizer').role(accountManager).skill(summarizeTenancy).models(sonnet);
const upsellDecision = H.halt('upsell-decision')
  .context(z.object({ customer: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .decision(z.object({ action: z.enum(['upsell', 'keep']) }));
const proposeUpsell = H.command('propose-upsell')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), plan: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ proposal: z.string() }))
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const created = await ctx.exec(['crm', 'propose-upsell', input.customer, input.plan]);
    return { proposal: created.stdout.trim() };
  });

const tenancyReview = H.flow('tenancy-review')
  .input(tenancySchema)
  .step('usage', usageReview, s => ({ customer: s.input.customer }))
  .step('summary', tenancySummarizer, s => ({ customer: s.input.customer, plan: s.input.plan, usage: s.usage.usage }))
  .halt('decision', upsellDecision, s => ({ customer: s.input.customer, summary: s.summary.summary }))
  .when(s => s.decision.action === 'upsell', f => f.step('upsell', proposeUpsell, s => ({ customer: s.input.customer, plan: s.input.plan })))
  .exit('reviewed');

const billingFeed = http.webhook({
  name: 'billing-feed',
  path: '/billing',
  port: H.slot.port(0),
  secret: H.env('BILLING_SECRET'),
  body: tenancySchema.extend({ tenancyId: z.string() }),
  key: b => b.tenancyId,
  data: b => ({ customer: b.customer, plan: b.plan, billing: b.billing, churned: b.churned }),
  mode: 'upsert',
});

const tenancies = H.lane('tenancies')
  .of(tenancy)
  .from(billingFeed)
  .store(sqlite.store(store))
  .handle(tenancyReview, {
    exits: { reviewed: current },
    retry: { retries: 2, backoff: { initial: '1h', factor: 2 }, exhausted: reviewFailed },
  });

const negotiationSchema = z.object({
  vendor: z.string(),
  item: z.string(),
  targetUsd: z.number(),
  expiresAt: z.string(),
  vendorMessage: z.string(),
  vendorStatus: z.enum(['opened', 'countered', 'accepted', 'walkedAway']),
});
const ourTurn = H.state('our-turn').pending();
const theirTurn = H.state('their-turn').waiting();
const agreed = H.state('agreed').terminal('success');
const weWalkedAway = H.state('we-walked-away').terminal('neutral');
const theyWalkedAway = H.state('they-walked-away').terminal('failure');
const expired = H.state('expired').terminal('failure');
const negotiationAbandoned = H.state('negotiation-abandoned').terminal('failure');
const negotiation = H.work('Negotiation').schema(negotiationSchema).states(ourTurn, theirTurn, agreed, weWalkedAway, theyWalkedAway, expired, negotiationAbandoned);

const negotiator = H.role('negotiator').promptFile('./prompts/negotiator.md');
const nextOffer = H.skill('next-offer')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), targetUsd: z.number(), vendorMessage: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ action: z.enum(['offer', 'walkAway']), offerUsd: z.number(), message: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Vendor ${i.vendor} on ${i.item} (target $${i.targetUsd}) said:\n${i.vendorMessage}\nDraft our next move.`);
const negotiatorSeat = H.seat('negotiator').role(negotiator).skill(nextOffer).models(sonnet);
const sendOffer = H.command('send-offer')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), offerUsd: z.number(), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ messageId: z.string() }))
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const sent = await ctx.exec(['procurement', 'send', input.vendor, String(input.offerUsd)], { stdin: input.message });
    return { messageId: sent.stdout.trim() };
  });

const negotiationRound = H.flow('negotiation-round')
  .input(negotiationSchema)
  .step('draft', negotiatorSeat, s => ({ vendor: s.input.vendor, item: s.input.item, targetUsd: s.input.targetUsd, vendorMessage: s.input.vendorMessage }))
  .when(s => s.draft.action === 'walkAway', f => f.exit('walkedAway'))
  .step('send', sendOffer, s => ({ vendor: s.input.vendor, offerUsd: s.draft.offerUsd, message: s.draft.message }))
  .exit('offered');

const vendorReplies = http.webhook({
  name: 'vendor-replies',
  path: '/vendor-replies',
  port: H.slot.port(0),
  secret: H.env('VENDOR_PORTAL_SECRET'),
  body: negotiationSchema.extend({ negotiationId: z.string() }),
  key: b => b.negotiationId,
  data: b => ({ vendor: b.vendor, item: b.item, targetUsd: b.targetUsd, expiresAt: b.expiresAt, vendorMessage: b.vendorMessage, vendorStatus: b.vendorStatus }),
  mode: 'update',
});

const negotiations = H.lane('negotiations')
  .of(negotiation)
  .from(manual('procurement-desk'), vendorReplies)
  .store(sqlite.store(store))
  .handle(negotiationRound, {
    exits: { offered: theirTurn, walkedAway: weWalkedAway },
    retry: { retries: 2, backoff: { initial: '10m', factor: 2 }, exhausted: negotiationAbandoned },
  })
  .wip(3);

const tenancyUpdates = H.events.updates(tenancies);
const vendorUpdates = H.events.updates(negotiations).where(e => e.unit.state === theirTurn.name);

const triggers = [
  H.trigger('monthly-tenancy-review')
    .on(H.time.every('0 9 1 * *'))
    .do(tenancies.move({ state: current }, reviewDue), tenancies.move({ state: reviewFailed }, reviewDue)),
  H.trigger('suspend-overdue-tenancy')
    .on(tenancyUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.billing === 'overdue' && e.previous.billing === 'paid' && !e.unit.data.churned))
    .do(tenancies.move(e => e.unit.key, suspended)),
  H.trigger('reinstate-paid-tenancy')
    .on(tenancyUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.billing === 'paid' && e.previous.billing === 'overdue' && e.unit.state === suspended.name))
    .do(tenancies.move(e => e.unit.key, current)),
  H.trigger('tenancy-churn')
    .on(tenancyUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.churned))
    .do(tenancies.cancel(e => e.unit.key, churned)),
  H.trigger('vendor-countered')
    .on(vendorUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.vendorStatus === 'countered'))
    .do(negotiations.move(e => e.unit.key, ourTurn)),
  H.trigger('vendor-accepted')
    .on(vendorUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.vendorStatus === 'accepted'))
    .do(negotiations.move(e => e.unit.key, agreed)),
  H.trigger('vendor-walked-away')
    .on(vendorUpdates.where(e => e.unit.data.vendorStatus === 'walkedAway'))
    .do(negotiations.move(e => e.unit.key, theyWalkedAway)),
  H.trigger('negotiation-expiry')
    .on(H.time.at(negotiations, d => new Date(d.expiresAt)))
    .do(negotiations.cancel(e => e.unit.key, expired)),
];

const lifecycleOrder = H.policy.units('lifecycle-order', c => {
  const inconclusiveReading = c.metrics.read(inconclusiveShare);
  const experimentsLast = inconclusiveReading.samples >= 10 && (inconclusiveReading.value ?? 0) > 0.5;
  const waitingExperiments = c.candidates.filter(experiments.holds);
  const others = c.candidates.filter(x => !experiments.holds(x));
  return experimentsLast ? [...others, ...waitingExperiments] : [...waitingExperiments, ...others];
});

const pool = H.pool('api', [api]).serves(haiku, sonnet).policy(policies.soonestReset());

export const lifecycles = H.harness('lifecycles')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('./.harness/ledger.sqlite'))
  .pools(pool)
  .lanes(experiments, tenancies, negotiations)
  .triggers(...triggers)
  .scheduler(lifecycleOrder)
  .grants(H.grant(claudeCode.client({ name: 'owner' }), H.ops.work.read, H.ops.work.write, H.ops.resolve(upsellDecision), H.ops.telemetry.read, H.ops.attempts.manage))
  .observe(observers.board({ path: './BOARD.md' }), observers.telemetry({ path: './TELEMETRY.md' }));

=== END ===

Decide per the rubric. Output only the JSON object. Deliberate briefly; every thinking token is paid for and the files are the deliverable.

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface. A step is a command, a model call, a batch of model calls, or an external job (submitted now, collected later by a poll or a callback: a cloud batch, a GPU run, a long service call); a batch and an external job hold no capacity while they run. (External jobs ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role, resource, halt). A resource (a file pattern, a database, a section, a host) is a named shared thing that leases, memory scope and metric facets reference by identity; a string never stands in for it. A halt is a named question with a decision schema that grants, metrics, timers and policies reference by identity. *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall, seat = role × models × choice policy: a seat holds a role with the model a deterministic policy picks at attempt time, an agent is a seat with one model, and metrics on an A/B comparison key on the seat so a model swap does not break the series). (Resources, halts and seats ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts. By default a failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy, and the lane's policy names where exhaustion leaves the unit, in the kind's own states; the kind declares nothing about failure. Where an active unit stands in its work is its attempt's current step, read from the ledger; a kind declares no states for it, and waiting on a human is the attempt's blocked state, recorded once. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why. The failure default was added after generation 1, when three of eleven children read the silence as "every kind declares a failure state" and invented states that loop or dead-end. Retry's end state moved to the lane, and the active position was ruled, on 2026-11-01 after run one: three generation-3 adversaries showed a move on the kind only means something given the lane's policy, and three generations modelled waiting on a human twice.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable, and it may be partitioned by backend. Account quota shared by several harnesses is a ledger partition of append-only quota events: each harness appends its own consumption and folds the window at read time, so no harness takes a lock over another's account state. The account names its quota partition, as every instance carries its backend; the ledger carries no option for it. A quota store that needs the ledger's single-writer lock, or a second store under the ledger's name, breaks this principle. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all. (Shared quota ruled 2026-11-01 after generation 1.)
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted; a grant names the halt it may resolve. A halt's resolver is a human, a registered policy (a deterministic function whose decision is recorded with the metrics and sample counts it read), or a clock: a timeout default that resolves the halt without cancelling the attempt. Deadlines on a halt run from the recorded halt, never from unit data. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished". A metric dimension is a typed ledger column (kind, lane, state, model, seat, resource, halt) or a declared facet entity; a facet that repeats a column is a startup error. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.


---

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).


---

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.


---

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.

- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.

Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.
