import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { linear } from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import { folder } from 'harness-dsl/folder';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { git } from 'harness-dsl/git';
import { local } from 'harness-dsl/local';
import { markdown } from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const workstation = local.runner('workstation').slots(4);

const sharedQuota = sqlite.quota('claude-quota', { path: '.harness/quota.sqlite' });
const claudeA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-a', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_A_TOKEN'), quota: sharedQuota });
const claudeB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-b', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_B_TOKEN'), quota: sharedQuota });
const claudeC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-c', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_C_TOKEN'), quota: sharedQuota });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'), quota: sharedQuota });

const soonestExpiring = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring', ({ candidates, now }) =>
  candidates
    .filter(
      (candidate) =>
        candidate.shareUsed < candidate.shareCap &&
        (candidate.cooldownUntil === undefined || candidate.cooldownUntil.getTime() <= now.getTime()),
    )
    .sort((a, b) => a.windowResetsAt.getTime() - b.windowResetsAt.getTime())[0],
);

const subscriptions = H.pool('subscriptions')
  .accounts(claudeA, claudeB, claudeC)
  .share(claudeA, 0.6)
  .share(claudeB, 0.5)
  .share(claudeC, 0.4)
  .drain(soonestExpiring)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('sonnet', { id: 'claude-sonnet-4-5' });
const opus = claudeCode.model('opus', { id: 'claude-opus-4-1' });

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-model', [sonnet, opus], ({ kind, seat, metrics }) => {
  const cheaper = metrics.attempts({ of: kind, seat, model: sonnet, window: { lastDays: 14 } });
  return cheaper.samples >= 20 && cheaper.successRate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .intents('read', 'edit', 'run', 'search')
  .instructions('Implement the work item in the worktree. Keep changes minimal and covered by tests.');
const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents('read', 'run', 'search', 'record')
  .instructions('Find deficits in the change. Report each deficit as one actionable sentence.');
const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .intents('read', 'search')
  .instructions('Decompose an epic into independently shippable features.');

const experience = H.memory('experience', 'experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste', 'taste');

const experienceJournal = H.journal('coding-experience', experience)
  .store(jsonl.memoryStore({ path: 'memory/experience.jsonl' }))
  .recall({ by: 'specificity', limit: 12 })
  .readBy(builderRole, auditorRole)
  .recordedBy(auditorRole);

const tasteJournal = H.journal('owner-taste', taste)
  .store(jsonl.memoryStore({ path: 'memory/taste.jsonl' }))
  .recall({ by: 'specificity', limit: 20 })
  .readBy(builderRole, plannerRole);

const ownerDecision = H.halt('owner-decision').decision(
  z.object({ choice: z.string(), note: z.string() }),
);

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks').argv(['npm', 'run', 'check']).runner(workstation);

const builder = H.seat('builder')
  .role(builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .pool(subscriptions)
  .workspace(git.worktree({ repo: '.', base: 'main' }))
  .guard({ leaseFiles: true, beforeStop: projectChecks })
  .halts(ownerDecision);

const auditor = H.seat('auditor')
  .role(auditorRole)
  .model(sonnet)
  .pool(subscriptions)
  .workspace(git.worktree({ repo: '.', base: 'main' }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }));

const planner = H.seat('planner')
  .role(plannerRole)
  .model(opus)
  .pool(subscriptions)
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() })) }));

const workSchema = z.object({ ref: z.string(), title: z.string(), body: z.string() });

const Todo = H.state('Todo', 'pending');
const Building = H.state('Building', 'active');
const Auditing = H.state('Auditing', 'active');
const Planning = H.state('Planning', 'active');
const AwaitingFeatures = H.state('AwaitingFeatures', 'waiting');
const Done = H.terminal('Done', 'success');
const Stuck = H.terminal('Stuck', 'failure');
const Cancelled = H.terminal('Cancelled', 'neutral');

const Bug = H.kind('Bug')
  .attributes(workSchema)
  .states(Todo, Building, Auditing, Done, Stuck, Cancelled)
  .key((bug) => bug.ref)
  .initial(Todo);

const Feature = H.kind('Feature')
  .attributes(workSchema)
  .states(Todo, Building, Auditing, Done, Stuck, Cancelled)
  .key((feature) => feature.ref)
  .initial(Todo);

const Epic = H.kind('Epic')
  .attributes(workSchema)
  .states(Todo, Planning, AwaitingFeatures, Done, Stuck, Cancelled)
  .key((epic) => epic.ref)
  .initial(Todo);

const Due = H.state('Due', 'pending');
const Probing = H.state('Probing', 'active');
const Healthy = H.terminal('Healthy', 'success');
const Unhealthy = H.terminal('Unhealthy', 'failure');
const Skipped = H.terminal('Skipped', 'neutral');

const Heartbeat = H.kind('ServiceHeartbeat')
  .attributes(z.object({ service: z.string(), scheduledAt: z.string() }))
  .states(Due, Probing, Healthy, Unhealthy, Skipped)
  .key((beat) => `${beat.service}@${beat.scheduledAt}`)
  .initial(Due);

const buildAndAudit = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .input(workSchema)
  .params(z.object({ rounds: z.number() }))
  .loop(
    'rounds',
    (round) =>
      round
        .step('build', builder, (ctx) => ({
          task: `Round ${ctx.iteration + 1}: implement "${ctx.unit.attributes.title}" and fix every deficit the auditor left in the worktree.\n${ctx.unit.attributes.body}`,
        }))
        .step('audit', auditor, (ctx) => ({
          task: `Audit the change for "${ctx.unit.attributes.title}". Builder notes: ${ctx.steps.build}`,
        })),
    {
      max: (ctx) => ctx.params.rounds,
      until: (ctx) => ctx.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0,
    },
  )
  .exit('clean', (ctx) => ctx.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0)
  .exit('roundsExhausted');

const decomposeEpic = H.flow('decompose-epic')
  .input(workSchema)
  .step('plan', planner, (ctx) => ({
    task: `Decompose the epic "${ctx.unit.attributes.title}" into features.\n${ctx.unit.attributes.body}`,
  }))
  .spawn('features', H.lane('features-placeholder', Feature), () => [])
  .exit('delivered');

const healthCheck = H.command('service-health')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string() }))
  .argv((input) => ['./scripts/health.sh', input.service])
  .runner(workstation);

const probe = H.flow('probe')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string(), scheduledAt: z.string() }))
  .step('probe', healthCheck, (ctx) => ({ service: ctx.unit.attributes.service }))
  .exit('healthy');

const trackerKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const tracker = linear.store({
  apiKey: trackerKey,
  team: 'PRODUCT',
  workflow: ['Todo', 'In Progress', 'In Review', 'Done', 'Blocked', 'Canceled'],
});

const services = ['api', 'worker', 'web'];

const heartbeats = H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat)
  .supply(H.clock('every-five-minutes').every({ minutes: 5 }), (tick, to) =>
    services.map((service) => to.create({ service, scheduledAt: tick.at.toISOString() })),
  )
  .handler(probe, { exits: { healthy: Healthy }, during: { probe: Probing } })
  .retry({ maxAttempts: 1, backoff: 'fixed', initialDelayMs: 0, exhausted: Unhealthy })
  .on(H.cancel, { enter: Skipped });

const bugs = H.lane('bugs', Bug)
  .supply(linear.issues({ apiKey: trackerKey, team: 'PRODUCT', labels: ['bug'] }), (issue, to) =>
    to.create({ ref: issue.identifier, title: issue.title, body: issue.description }),
  )
  .supply(folder.files({ path: 'inbox/bugs', glob: '*.md' }), (file, to) =>
    to.create({ ref: file.path, title: file.name, body: file.body }),
  )
  .supply(H.operator)
  .store(tracker, {
    Todo: 'Todo',
    Building: 'In Progress',
    Auditing: 'In Review',
    Done: 'Done',
    Stuck: 'Blocked',
    Cancelled: 'Canceled',
  })
  .handler(buildAndAudit, {
    exits: { clean: Done, roundsExhausted: Stuck },
    during: { build: Building, audit: Auditing },

# harness-dsl: ours-2, materialized

This is the owner's ruled design of 2026-11-01, written as a surface that compiles. Where the battery forced a change, the change is the smallest one that keeps every principle. Each change is listed under *What changed and why*.

## Entities

### Kinds (pure vocabulary, no backend)

| Builder | Produces |
|---|---|
| `H.work(name).schema(z).states(...)` | A work kind: its data shape and its named states. Nothing else. |
| `H.state(name).pending() / .active() / .waiting() / .terminal(verdict)` | A shareable state with its skeleton position. A terminal state also carries its verdict: `success`, `failure` or `neutral`, with no default. A kind has at most one active state. |
| `H.resource(name)` | A named shared thing: a file area, a database, a section or a host. |
| `H.halt(name).context(z).ask(text \| fn).decision(z)` | A named question with a typed context and a decision schema. |
| `H.memory(name).content(z).trust('experience' \| 'taste')` | A memory kind. The kernel owns the envelope: id, created, status, and `when: { kinds, roles, skills, resources }`, where every field is an entity reference. |
| `H.role(name).prompt / promptFile / intents / recall / record / use` | What an agent knows and may do. |
| `H.skill(name).input(z).output(z).prompt(fn).assert(fn).maxRetries(n)` | A typed contract for one model call. |
| `H.facet(name)` | A metric dimension that is not a ledger column. |

### Instances (carry a backend)

| Builder | Backend |
|---|---|
| `H.account(name, driver).maxQuotaShare(r).quota(partition)` | A `ModelDriver`. Quota lives in a `QuotaPartition` that the account names. |
| `H.model(id, options).pricing(pricing)` | A `Pricing`. A model is not bound to an account or a pool. |
| `H.runner.local(name, { slots })`, `H.runner.ssh(name, {...})`, `.env({...})` | A `Runner`. Slots are capacity. |
| `H.command(name).input.output.runner.effect.detect.run` | A deterministic executable. `effect` declares its restart behaviour. |
| `H.job(name).input.output.submit.collect.poll` | An external job: submitted, then collected by poll. It holds no slot and no WIP while it runs. |

### Pivots (each has a noun)

| Pivot | Connects | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| **pool** `H.pool(name, accounts).serves(...).policy(p).fallback(a)` | accounts × policy × models served | the account for one invocation |
| **seat** `H.seat(name).role(r).models(...).policy(p)` | role × models × choice policy | the model for one attempt; metrics key on the seat |
| **agent** `H.agent(name).role(r).model(m)` | a seat with one model | the same entity sort (`seat`), so metrics do not change if it later becomes a seat |
| **lane** `H.lane(name).of(kind).from(...).store(s).handle(flow, map?).exits({...}).retry({...}).wip(n).ceiling({...}).facet(f, fn).after(fn, {...})` | work kind × suppliers × store × handler | the lane's units and attempts |
| **journal** `H.journal(name).of(memoryKind).store(ms).recall(policy)` | memory kind × store × recall | the recalled items for one invocation |
| **grant** `H.grant(client, ...operations)` | client × operations | one client's rights on the control API |
| **trigger** `H.trigger(name).on(source).when(pred).do(...consequences)` | a recorded source × consequences | recorded firings |
| **flow** `H.flow(name)...` | executables in order | the handler of a lane |

Executables are `Command`, `Job` and `Call`. A `Call` is made by `seat.call(skill)` or `agent.call(skill)`. All three compose through `Executable<I, O>`. A batch of model calls is `.batch(name, { items, call })` inside a flow, and it is submitted through the account driver's batch capability.

### Vocabulary of words

- **run**: one harness process lifetime under one ledger claim.
- **attempt**: one execution of a lane's flow for a unit. Its outcome is succeeded, failed or cancelled.
- **step**: one addressed node of a flow (`step`, `halt`, `batch`, `spawn`, or a loop iteration). Its address is `flowName/path` plus the flow hash.
- **invocation**: one model call.

## Rules

### Lifecycle

- A unit is at pending, active, waiting or terminal. The scheduler and the board use these positions. An active unit's progress is its attempt's current step, read from the ledger.
- A flow names no state. It ends in `.exit(label)`, where the label is static or chosen by a selector. The lane maps every label to a kind state, or to `{ to, maxTimes, then }`. That form is a declared re-entry bound, which the kernel counts per unit.
  - An unmapped label is a type error.
  - A state outside the kind is a type error where TypeScript can express it, and a startup error otherwise.
- A failed attempt leaves the unit pending under `lane.retry({ tries, backoff, delaySeconds, exhausted })`. A lane without `retry` is a startup error. When retries are exhausted, the unit moves to the `exhausted` state.
- A step may carry two options:
  - `{ retry }` retries the step inside the attempt.
  - `{ onFailure: 'block' }` blocks the attempt with reason `stepFailure` and carries the step's error output.
- Blocked is an attempt state. Its reasons are `decision`, `stepFailure`, `budget`, `interrupted` and `definitionChanged`.
  - A blocked attempt holds no slot and no WIP.
  - Its unit shows at `waiting` on the board, with the blocked row beside it.
  - The same holds while a job, batch or spawn is outstanding.
- **Signals.** When a supplier offer's key matches an open unit, the offer updates that unit. `updatesOnly()` suppliers send `Update<Partial<D>>`; other suppliers send full data. What happens next depends on where the unit is:
  - While a step runs, the update is deferred to the next attempt.
  - While the attempt is blocked on a halt, the attempt is cancelled (reason `interrupted`) and the unit returns to pending.
  - While the unit is at a waiting state, it returns to pending.
- `lane.move(state)` is the one consequence that moves a unit from outside. It cancels any open attempt and records the move. Operator cancellation is a `move` through `H.ops.work.write`.
- `lane.after(fn, { failed })` orders units. A unit whose predecessor key is not yet terminal with a success verdict is not a scheduling candidate. If the predecessor ends at a failure verdict, the unit moves to `failed`, and the predecessor is recorded as the reason.

### Facets

- `lane.facet(f, fn)` writes a facet value derived from unit data onto every event of the lane's units.
- `flow.facet(f, fn)` writes a facet value derived from the flow state, including earlier steps. The value applies from that point in the attempt onward and is kept on the unit.
- A facet names an entity, never a column.

### Halts

- `.halt(stepName, halt, context)`: the step name is the address and the halt is the question. One halt entity may appear at several addresses.
- A halt has three kinds of resolver:
  - **Human**: through a grant on `H.ops.resolve(halt)`.
  - **Policy**: through `H.ops.resolve(halt).by(H.policy.halt(...))`, as a trigger consequence on `halt.opened()`.
  - **Clock**: through `.with(fn)`, on `halt.opened().after(d)` or `.at(fn)`. Clock deadlines run from the recorded `halt.opened` event.
- Every resolution records its resolver sort (`human`, `policy` or `clock`) and its client.
- A clock resolution does not cancel the attempt. The flow continues from the halt with the decision.
- `halt.resolved()` is a source. Its payload carries the context, the decision, the resolver and the client. This is how outcomes of human decisions become memory candidates without an agent tool.

### Policies

A policy is one entity with five typed constructors: `H.policy.pool`, `.seat`, `.schedule`, `.recall` and `.halt`.

- Every policy is deterministic.
- Every metric read through `metrics.read` or `metrics.group` is recorded, with its value and sample count, on `policy.decided`.
- A schedule policy returns an ordered subset of the candidates. Omitted candidates do not start this tick.

### Metrics

- A metric is `H.metric(name).rate(hits, of) | count | sum | mean | median`, computed over `H.events.*` sets.
- Dimensions are typed `Column`s or declared `Facet`s.
- `where: { seat | model }` selects events of attempts in which that seat or model was invoked.
- Every reading is `{ value, samples }`.
- `metric.crossing({ below, above, samples, window, by })` gives two sources, `falls()` and `rises()`, for hysteresis.
  - Each source fires once on entering its band: below `below`, or above `above`.
  - It fires per `by` key.
  - It fires only after the opposite band was entered, or on the first qualifying reading.
- `harness.metrics(...)` publishes metrics to telemetry observers and to the control API's telemetry operation. A metric read only by a policy or a crossing is registered through that reference and need not be listed.

### Memory

- Journals own the store and the recall policy. Roles name the memory kinds they recall and record.
- Recall scope is the attempt's kind, the role, the skill and the flow's declared `.resources(...)`.
- An item recorded by a trigger or a command is `status: 'candidate'` when the mapper says so. Recall reads only `accepted` items.
- Curation (`accept`, `merge`, `drop`) is `H.ops.memory.curate(journal)`.

### Resources and leases

- `flow.resources(select)` returns plain resources, which only set memory scope, or `H.lease.exclusive(r)` / `H.lease.shared(r)`.
- Leases are ledger state (`lease.requested`, `lease.acquired`, `lease.released`).
  - A lease is acquired before the first step and held through the attempt.
  - It is released when the attempt ends, or when the attempt blocks on a halt for longer than its lease.
- Agent plugins may lease at write time through `PluginContext.lease`.
- `plugins.fileLeaseGuard([{ resource, globs }])` maps resources to file patterns by identity.

### Resumption (the scenario 10 mechanism)

The mechanism is replay over a memoizing ledger.

1. On start, the harness claims the ledger, which has a single writer.
   - A second instance is refused.
   - The exception is a holder whose heartbeat is stale. Then the new instance takes over and records the takeover.
2. Each open attempt replays its flow. Every address with a `completed` record returns its recorded output at no cost.
3. The address that was `started` at the crash is handled by its executable:
   - `repeatable` reruns.
   - `unrepeatable` calls `detect` if one is declared, and otherwise blocks the attempt (`interrupted`).
   - A `Call` asks its driver's `recover`.
   - A `Job` or a batch with a recorded ref is collected.
   - A halt reads its resolution.
   - A spawn reads its children.
4. A changed flow hash at a recorded address blocks the attempt (`definitionChanged`). The supervisor restarts it from the top or abandons it.
5. Loop iterations are addresses, so a loop of batches resumes at the next iteration.

The author writes nothing for any of this.

### Quota

- Each account names a `QuotaPartition`.
- Drivers report quota through `DriverContext.reportQuota`. The kernel appends events and folds the window at read time.
- Harnesses that name the same partition share it. No harness locks another.

### Startup validation (`start()` rejects)

- Duplicate names within one entity sort.
- A lane without `retry`.
- An exit or retry target outside the lane's kind.
- A kind with two active states, or a terminal state without a verdict.
- A trigger, grant or journal that refers to an unregistered lane, journal or halt.
- A facet named like a column.
- A seat or agent whose models no registered pool serves.
- A role that recalls a memory kind no registered journal holds.
- A `fileLeaseGuard` that is missing a resource which a flow leases or a memory item scopes.
- A step address used twice in one flow.
- A batch whose account driver lacks batch support.

## What changed and why

1. **Halt step address** (weakness 3): the step is now `.halt(stepName, halt, context)`, so the address and the entity are distinct.
2. **Halt context**: `H.halt(...).context(z)` types what `ask`, policies and clocks read. Without it, the timeout decision of scenario 11 cannot be typed.
3. **Policy constructors**: `H.policy.pool/seat/schedule/recall/halt`. A policy is still one entity sort, but its input is now inferred without annotation (principle 20).
4. **Supervisor merged into grant**: `H.supervisor` is removed. A supervisor is a `Client` from an adapter (`claudeCode.client`, `http.client`), and the client names its transport (weakness 8). One session pointed at two harnesses is two clients with the same session name.
5. **`unit.cancel()` replaced by `lane.move(state)`**: a cancellation must land somewhere in the kind's states. One consequence now covers cancel, expire and park.
6. **`lane.due(fn)`** is the per-unit time source. Deadlines from unit data re-arm on every recorded update, which covers the scenario 9 SLA extension. `H.time` and `H.signal` are removed, because the battery uses them only through suppliers and `due`.
7. **`lane.exits` source renamed**: the brief had `lane.exits` as both the exit map and a source. The source is gone (it was unused); `enters` remains.
8. **Crossing** returns `falls()` and `rises()` sources for hysteresis.
9. **Exit bounds** `{ to, maxTimes, then }` express scenario 11's return limit without counting in the flow.
10. **`lane.after`** orders units (scenario 12), and **`lane.facet`** sets facet values. Both are lane settings because both are about the lane's units.
11. **`flow.resources`** carries leases and memory scope (scenario 12 locks, scenario 6 sections). `flow.use` is removed; plugins live on roles.
12. **`handle(flow, map)`**: the lane maps unit data to flow input, so one flow serves Bug (3 rounds) and Feature (5).
13. **Loop carry**: `initial` and `next` carry typed state between iterations. Iterations are addresses.
14. **Supply builder**: `Supply<D>.map/key/updatesOnly`. Update-only suppliers emit `Partial<D>`.
15. **`fileLeaseGuard`** takes `{ resource, globs }` by identity and is checked at start (weakness 4, partially).
16. **`anthropic.batch()` removed**: batch submission is a driver capability, and batch pricing is `Usage.batch` in `Pricing`. This narrows weakness 2: a batch is a job that the driver knows how to submit.
17. **`flow.facet(facet, fn)`** (scenario 2). The support conversation's category is decided by the classifier step, not by the helpdesk, so no lane-level facet over unit data can carry it.
    - Without a flow-level facet, "approval rate by category" and the safe-category policy (`where: { facet }`) have nothing to read.
    - The value is written onto subsequent events of the attempt and kept on the unit.
    - `lane.facet` remains for facets that derive from unit data.
18. **`halt.resolved()` source** (scenarios 2 and 6). Taste grows from a human's decision: the reviewer's edit in scenario 2, the editor's notes in scenario 6. That decision lives on the halt resolution, not in unit data, so a trigger on a state entry cannot see it.
    - A resolution source keeps memory capture a trigger consequence (principle 13), with no agent tool and no command that copies the decision.
    - It needs one new kernel payload type, `HaltResolved<C, D>`. It is fired from the recorded `halt.resolved` ledger event.
19. **`harness.metrics(...)`** (scenarios 9, 11 and 12). Each of these scenarios asks for metrics that are read by people, not by a policy or a crossing: median time to decision per halt, retries per lane, timeout share of signoffs, GPU job seconds in flight, and lock wait per database.
    - Before this change, a metric existed only through a reference from a policy or a crossing. Nothing told the telemetry observer or the auditor's `telemetry.read` that these metrics exist.
    - Registering them on the harness is the only change. Their definitions are unchanged, and their names are checked for duplicates at start with the other entities.

    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: O }, E, X>;
    when<A2, E2 extends string = never>(
      predicate: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => boolean,
      branch: (flow: Flow<I, A, never, X>) => FlowShape<I, A2, E2, X>,
    ): Flow<I, A & Partial<Omit<A2, keyof A>>, E | E2, X>;
    loop<N extends string, C, A2, E2 extends string = never>(
      name: N,
      spec: {
        readonly maxIterations: number | ((state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => number);
        readonly initial: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => C;
        readonly body: (flow: Flow<I, A, never, X & LoopScope<C>>) => FlowShape<I, A2, E2, X & LoopScope<C>>;
        readonly next: (state: FlowState<I, A2, X & LoopScope<C>>) => C;
        readonly until: (state: FlowState<I, A2, X & LoopScope<C>>) => boolean;
      },
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: LoopResult<C> }, E | E2, X>;
    batch<N extends string, T, O>(
      name: N,
      spec: {
        readonly items: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => readonly NoInfer<T>[];
        readonly call: Call<T, O>;
      },
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: readonly O[] }, E, X>;
    halt<N extends string, C, D>(
      name: N,
      halt: Halt<C, D>,
      context: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => NoInfer<C>,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: D }, E, X>;
    halt<N extends string, D>(name: N, halt: Halt<void, D>): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: D }, E, X>;
    spawn<N extends string, CD>(
      name: N,
      lane: LaneRef<CD>,
      items: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => readonly NoInfer<CD>[],
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: readonly K.ChildResult[] }, E, X>;
    exit<L extends string>(label: L | ((state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => L)): ExitedFlow<I, A, E | L, X>;
  }

  export interface Supply<D> extends K.EntityRef<'supply'> {
    readonly __supplies?: D;
    map<D2>(map: (raw: D) => D2): Supply<D2>;
    key(key: (data: D) => string): Supply<D>;
    updatesOnly(): Update<D>;
  }

  export interface Update<D> extends K.EntityRef<'supply'> {
    readonly __updates?: D;
  }

  export interface ExitBound<St extends State> {
    readonly to: St;
    readonly maxTimes: number;
    readonly then: St;
  }

  export interface LaneRef<D> extends K.EntityRef<'lane'> {
    readonly __accepts?: (data: D) => void;
  }

  export interface Lane<D, St extends State, E extends string = never> extends LaneRef<D> {
    from(...suppliers: ReadonlyArray<Supply<D> | Update<Partial<D>>>): Lane<D, St, E>;
    store(store: K.Store): Lane<D, St, E>;
    handle<E2 extends string>(flow: ExitedFlow<D, object, E2>): Lane<D, St, E2>;
    handle<I, E2 extends string>(flow: ExitedFlow<I, object, E2>, map: (unit: K.UnitView<D>) => I): Lane<D, St, E2>;
    exits(map: { readonly [L in E]: St | ExitBound<St> }): Lane<D, St, E>;
    retry(retry: K.Retry & { readonly exhausted: St }): Lane<D, St, E>;
    wip(limit: number): Lane<D, St, E>;
    ceiling(ceiling: {
      readonly maxUsd: number;
      readonly onExceed: Halt<K.CeilingContext, K.CeilingDecision> | 'fail';
    }): Lane<D, St, E>;
    facet(facet: Facet, value: (data: D) => string): Lane<D, St, E>;
    after(predecessor: (data: D) => string | undefined, options: { readonly failed: St }): Lane<D, St, E>;
    unitOf(candidate: K.Candidate): K.UnitView<D> | undefined;
    enters(...states: readonly St[]): Source<K.Entered<D>>;
    streak(state: St, count: number, options?: { readonly by?: Facet }): Source<K.Streak<D>>;
    due(deadline: (unit: K.UnitView<D>) => Date | undefined): Source<K.Due<D>>;
    create<P>(map: (payload: P) => D, key?: (payload: P) => string): Consequence<P>;
    move(state: St): Consequence<{ readonly unit: K.UnitRef }>;
    move<P>(state: St, key: (payload: P) => string): Consequence<P>;
    pause(reason: string): Consequence<unknown>;
    resume(): Consequence<unknown>;
  }

  export interface LaneStart {
    of<D, St extends State>(kind: WorkKind<D, St>): Lane<D, St>;
  }

  export interface Journal<C> extends K.JournalRef<C> {
    store(store: K.MemoryStore): Journal<C>;
    recall(policy: RecallPolicy): Journal<C>;
    record<P>(map: (payload: P) => K.MemoryDraft<C>): Consequence<P>;
  }

  export interface JournalStart {
    of<C>(kind: MemoryKind<C>): Journal<C>;
  }

  export interface Trigger<P> extends K.EntityRef<'trigger'> {
    when(predicate: (payload: P) => boolean): Trigger<P>;
    do(...consequences: ReadonlyArray<Consequence<P>>): Trigger<P>;
  }

  export interface TriggerStart {
    on<P>(source: Source<P>): Trigger<P>;
  }

  export interface Operation extends K.EntityRef<'operation'> {}

  export interface Resolve<C, D> extends Operation {
    with(decide: (payload: K.HaltOpened<C>) => D): Consequence<K.HaltOpened<C>>;
    by(policy: Policy<K.HaltPolicyInput<C>, D | undefined>): Consequence<K.HaltOpened<C>>;
  }

  export interface Grant extends K.EntityRef<'grant'> {
    readonly client: K.Client;
    readonly operations: readonly Operation[];
  }

  export interface Scheduler extends K.EntityRef<'scheduler'> {
    policy(policy: SchedulePolicy): Scheduler;
  }

  export interface Harness extends K.EntityRef<'harness'> {
    ledger(ledger: K.Ledger): Harness;
    pools(...pools: readonly Pool[]): Harness;
    lanes(...lanes: ReadonlyArray<LaneRef<never>>): Harness;
    journals(...journals: ReadonlyArray<K.JournalRef<never>>): Harness;
    triggers(...triggers: ReadonlyArray<K.EntityRef<'trigger'>>): Harness;
    scheduler(scheduler: Scheduler): Harness;
    grants(...grants: readonly Grant[]): Harness;
    metrics(...metrics: readonly Metric[]): Harness;
    observe(...observers: readonly K.Observer[]): Harness;
    start(): Promise<K.RunningHarness>;
  }

  export const H: {
    work(name: string): WorkKind<unknown, never>;
    state<N extends string>(name: N): StateBuilder<N>;
    resource(name: string): Resource;
    halt(name: string): Halt<void, unknown>;
    memory(name: string): MemoryKind<unknown>;
    role(name: string): Role;
    skill(name: string): Skill<void, unknown>;
    facet(name: string): Facet;

    account(name: string, driver: K.ModelDriver): Account;
    model(modelId: string, options?: ModelOptions): Model;
    runner: {
      local(name: string, options: { readonly slots: number }): Runner;
      ssh(name: string, options: {
        readonly host: K.Setting;
        readonly user: K.Setting;
        readonly key: K.EnvRef;
        readonly slots: number;
      }): Runner;
    };
    command(name: string): Command<void, void>;
    job(name: string): Job<void, void>;

    pool(name: string, accounts: readonly Account[]): Pool;
    seat(name: string): Seat;
    agent(name: string): Agent;
    lane(name: string): LaneStart;
    journal(name: string): JournalStart;
    grant(client: K.Client, ...operations: readonly Operation[]): Grant;

    flow(name: string): Flow<void, {}, never>;
    lease: {
      exclusive(resource: Resource): Lease;
      shared(resource: Resource): Lease;
    };
    trigger(name: string): TriggerStart;
    policy: {
      pool(name: string, decide: (input: K.PoolPolicyInput) => readonly K.AccountView[]): PoolPolicy;
      seat(name: string, decide: (input: K.SeatPolicyInput) => readonly K.ModelRef[]): SeatPolicy;
      schedule(name: string, decide: (input: K.SchedulePolicyInput) => readonly K.Candidate[]): SchedulePolicy;
      recall(name: string, decide: (input: K.RecallInput) => readonly K.RecallCandidate[]): RecallPolicy;
      halt<C, D>(
        name: string,
        halt: Halt<C, D>,
        decide: (input: K.HaltPolicyInput<C>) => NoInfer<D> | undefined,
      ): Policy<K.HaltPolicyInput<C>, D | undefined>;
    };
    metric(name: string): MetricBuilder;
    events: {
      attempts(filter?: { readonly outcome?: K.AttemptOutcome }): K.EventSet;
      terminal(filter?: { readonly verdict?: K.Verdict }): K.EventSet;
      entered(...states: readonly State[]): K.EventSet;
      created(): K.EventSet;
      steps(step: string, filter?: { readonly outcome?: K.AttemptOutcome }): K.EventSet;
      decisions<C, D>(halt: Halt<C, D>, filter?: {
        readonly match?: (decision: D) => boolean;
        readonly resolver?: K.ResolverSort;
      }): K.EventSet;
      invocations(filter?: { readonly outcome?: 'succeeded' | 'failed' }): K.EventSet;
      pauses(): K.EventSet;
      jobs(): K.EventSet;
      leases(): K.EventSet;
    };
    scheduler(): Scheduler;
    harness(name: string): Harness;

    ops: {
      resolve<C, D>(halt: Halt<C, D>): Resolve<C, D>;
      work: { readonly read: Operation; readonly write: Operation };
      memory: {
        write(...journals: ReadonlyArray<K.JournalRef<never>>): Operation;
        curate(...journals: ReadonlyArray<K.JournalRef<never>>): Operation;
      };
      telemetry: { readonly read: Operation };
      accounts: { readonly manage: Operation };
    };
    operation<I, O>(name: string, command: Command<I, O>): Operation;

    env(name: string): K.EnvRef;
    slot: { port(index: number): K.PortRef };
  };
}

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { linear } from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import { supply } from 'harness-dsl/supply';
import { policies } from 'harness-dsl/policies';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';
import { plugins } from 'harness-dsl/plugins';

const queued = H.state('queued').pending();
const building = H.state('building').active();
const ownerReview = H.state('ownerReview').waiting();
const done = H.state('done').terminal('success');
const abandoned = H.state('abandoned').terminal('failure');
const cancelled = H.state('cancelled').terminal('neutral');
const due = H.state('due').pending();
const checking = H.state('checking').active();
const healthy = H.state('healthy').terminal('success');
const unhealthy = H.state('unhealthy').terminal('failure');

const issueSchema = z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string(), reference: z.string().optional() });
const heartbeatSchema = z.object({ service: z.string(), at: z.string() });

const epic = H.work('Epic').schema(issueSchema).states(queued, building, done, abandoned, cancelled);
const feature = H.work('Feature').schema(issueSchema).states(queued, building, ownerReview, done, abandoned, cancelled);
const bug = H.work('Bug').schema(issueSchema).states(queued, building, ownerReview, done, abandoned, cancelled);
const serviceHeartbeat = H.work('ServiceHeartbeat').schema(heartbeatSchema).states(due, checking, healthy, unhealthy);

const payments = H.resource('payments');
const web = H.resource('web');
const platform = H.resource('platform');
const areas = [payments, web, platform];

const ruleSchema = z.object({ action: z.string(), condition: z.string(), reason: z.string() });
const experience = H.memory('experience').content(ruleSchema).trust('experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste').content(z.object({ preference: z.string() })).trust('taste');

const experienceJournal = H.journal('experience')
  .of(experience)
  .store(jsonl.store('memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 12 }));
const tasteJournal = H.journal('taste')
  .of(taste)
  .store(jsonl.store('memory/taste.jsonl'))
  .recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 8 }));

const workstation = H.runner.local('workstation', { slots: 4 });

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks')
  .runner(workstation)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (_input, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh('npm run check');
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
  });

const productionHealth = H.command('production-health')
  .output(z.object({ healthy: z.boolean(), status: z.number() }))
  .runner(workstation)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (_input, ctx) => {
    const response = await fetch(ctx.resolve(H.env('PRODUCTION_HEALTH_URL')), { signal: ctx.signal });
    return { healthy: response.ok, status: response.status };
  });

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .promptFile('prompts/builder.md')
  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience, taste)
  .use(
    plugins.gitWorktreeIsolation(),
    plugins.fileLeaseGuard([
      { resource: payments, globs: ['src/payments/**'] },
      { resource: web, globs: ['src/web/**'] },
      { resource: platform, globs: ['src/platform/**', 'package.json'] },
    ]),
    plugins.stopCheck(projectChecks),
  );
const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .promptFile('prompts/auditor.md')
  .intents(['read', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience)
  .record(experience);
const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .promptFile('prompts/planner.md')
  .intents(['read'])
  .recall(taste);

const quota = H.env('SHARED_QUOTA_PATH');
const quotaPartition = sqlite.quota('shared/quota.db');
const subscription = (name: string, configDirVariable: string, share: number) =>
  H.account(name, claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env(configDirVariable) }))
    .maxQuotaShare(share)
    .quota(quotaPartition);

const claudeOne = subscription('claude-one', 'CLAUDE_ONE_CONFIG', 0.6);
const claudeTwo = subscription('claude-two', 'CLAUDE_TWO_CONFIG', 0.6);
const claudeThree = subscription('claude-three', 'CLAUDE_THREE_CONFIG', 0.4);
const apiAccount = H.account('anthropic-api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') })).quota(quotaPartition);

const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const opus = H.model('claude-opus-4-1').pricing(anthropic.pricing());

const subscriptions = H.pool('subscriptions', [claudeOne, claudeTwo, claudeThree])
  .serves(sonnet, opus)
  .policy(policies.soonestExpiring())
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const kindSuccessRate = H.metric('kind-success-rate').rate(
  H.events.terminal({ verdict: 'success' }),
  H.events.terminal(),
);

const cheaperUntilItSlips = H.policy.seat('cheaper-until-it-slips', ({ unit, metrics }) => {
  const cheaper = metrics.read(kindSuccessRate, { window: '14d', where: { kind: unit.kind, model: sonnet } });
  const trusted = cheaper.samples < 20 || cheaper.value === undefined || cheaper.value >= 0.85;
  return trusted ? [sonnet, opus] : [opus, sonnet];
});

const builder = H.seat('builder').role(builderRole).models(sonnet, opus).policy(cheaperUntilItSlips);
const auditor = H.agent('auditor').role(auditorRole).model(sonnet);
const planner = H.agent('planner').role(plannerRole).model(opus);

const build = H.skill('build')
  .input(z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    description: z.string(),
    deficits: z.array(z.string()),
    guidance: z.string().optional(),
  }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), question: z.string().optional() }))
  .prompt(i => `Build: ${i.title}\n\n${i.description}\n\nOpen deficits:\n${i.deficits.join('\n')}\n\nOwner guidance: ${i.guidance ?? 'none'}`);

const audit = H.skill('audit')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(i => `Audit the change for "${i.title}". Builder summary:\n${i.summary}\nList every deficit that remains.`);

const planEpic = H.skill('plan-epic')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt(i => `Decompose the epic "${i.title}" into features.\n\n${i.description}`);

const ownerDecision = H.halt('owner-decision')
  .context(z.object({ title: z.string(), question: z.string() }))
  .ask(c => `${c.title}: ${c.question}`)
  .decision(z.object({ answer: z.string() }));

type Rounds = { readonly deficits: string[]; readonly guidance: string | undefined };

const deliver = H.flow('deliver')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string(), rounds: z.number() }))
  .resources(s => areas.filter(area => s.input.description.toLowerCase().includes(area.name)))
  .loop('rounds', {
    maxIterations: s => s.input.rounds,
    initial: (): Rounds => ({ deficits: [], guidance: undefined }),
    body: round => round
      .step('build', builder.call(build), s => ({
        title: s.input.title,
        description: s.input.description,
        deficits: s.carry.deficits,
        guidance: s.carry.guidance,
      }))
      .when(s => s.steps.build.question !== undefined, ask => ask
        .halt('ownerDecision', ownerDecision, s => ({ title: s.input.title, question: s.steps.build.question ?? '' })))
      .step('audit', auditor.call(audit), s => ({ title: s.input.title, summary: s.steps.build.summary })),
    next: s => ({ deficits: s.steps.audit.deficits, guidance: s.steps.ownerDecision?.answer ?? s.carry.guidance }),
    until: s => s.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0,
  })
  .exit(s => (s.steps.rounds.completed ? 'delivered' : 'roundsExhausted'));

const linearKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const tracker = linear.store({
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'ENG',
  statuses: [
    [queued, 'Todo'],
    [building, 'In Progress'],
    [ownerReview, 'In Review'],
    [done, 'Done'],
    [abandoned, 'Canceled'],
    [cancelled, 'Canceled'],
  ],
});
const fromTracker = (label: string) =>
  linear.issues({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'ENG', labels: [label] })
    .map(issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, reference: issue.identifier }))
    .key(data => data.reference);

const bugs = H.lane('bugs')
  .of(bug)
  .from(fromTracker('bug'), supply.folder({ path: 'inbox/bugs', schema: issueSchema }), supply.manual())
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(deliver, unit => ({ title: unit.data.title, description: unit.data.description, rounds: 3 }))
  .exits({ delivered: done, roundsExhausted: ownerReview })
  .retry({ tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: abandoned })
  .wip(2);

const features = H.lane('features')
  .of(feature)
  .from(fromTracker('feature'), supply.manual())
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(deliver, unit => ({ title: unit.data.title, description: unit.data.description, rounds: 5 }))
  .exits({ delivered: done, roundsExhausted: ownerReview })
  .retry({ tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: abandoned });

const decompose = H.flow('decompose')
  .input(issueSchema)
  .step('plan', planner.call(planEpic), s => ({ title: s.input.title, description: s.input.description }))
  .spawn('features', features, s => s.steps.plan.features.map(f => ({ title: f.title, description: f.description })))
  .exit(s => (s.steps.features.every(child => child.verdict === 'success') ? 'completed' : 'incomplete'));

const epics = H.lane('epics')
  .of(epic)
  .from(fromTracker('epic'))
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(decompose)
  .exits({ completed: done, incomplete: abandoned })

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { http } from 'harness-dsl/http';
import { supply } from 'harness-dsl/supply';
import { policies } from 'harness-dsl/policies';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';

const apiAccount = H.account('anthropic-api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }));
const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const apiPool = H.pool('api', [apiAccount]).serves(sonnet).policy(policies.soonestExpiring());

const store = sqlite.store('.harness/units.sqlite');
const workstation = H.runner.local('workstation', { slots: 4 });
const databaseRunner = H.runner
  .local('database-runner', { slots: 4 })
  .env({ ORDERS_DB_URL: H.env('ORDERS_DB_URL'), ANALYTICS_DB_URL: H.env('ANALYTICS_DB_URL') });

const databaseName = z.enum(['orders', 'analytics']);
const databases = { orders: H.resource('orders-db'), analytics: H.resource('analytics-db') };
const urlVariable = { orders: 'ORDERS_DB_URL', analytics: 'ANALYTICS_DB_URL' };

const queued = H.state('queued').pending();
const working = H.state('working').active();
const finished = H.state('finished').terminal('success');
const failed = H.state('failed').terminal('failure');
const parked = H.state('parked').waiting();
const cancelled = H.state('cancelled').terminal('neutral');

const evalSchema = z.object({ evalId: z.string(), checkpoint: z.string(), suite: z.string() });
const evalRunKind = H.work('EvalRun').schema(evalSchema).states(queued, working, finished, failed, cancelled);

const gpuApi = H.env('GPU_API_URL');
const gpuToken = H.env('GPU_API_TOKEN');

const prepare = H.command('prepare-eval')
  .input(evalSchema)
  .output(z.object({ bundle: z.string() }))
  .runner(workstation)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(`./prepare.sh ${i.checkpoint} ${i.suite}`);
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
    return { bundle: result.stdout.trim() };
  });

const gpuEvaluation = H.job('gpu-evaluation')
  .input(z.object({ evalId: z.string(), bundle: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ resultsUri: z.string() }))
  .submit(async (i, ctx) => {
    const response = await fetch(`${ctx.resolve(gpuApi)}/jobs`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${ctx.resolve(gpuToken)}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: i.evalId, bundle: i.bundle }),
    });
    return z.object({ jobId: z.string() }).parse(await response.json()).jobId;
  })
  .collect(async (ref, ctx) => {
    const response = await fetch(`${ctx.resolve(gpuApi)}/jobs/${ref}`, {
      headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${ctx.resolve(gpuToken)}` },
    });
    const job = z
      .object({
        state: z.enum(['queued', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed']),
        resultsUri: z.string().optional(),
        error: z.string().optional(),
      })
      .parse(await response.json());
    if (job.state === 'succeeded') return { status: 'done', output: { resultsUri: job.resultsUri ?? '' } };
    if (job.state === 'failed') return { status: 'failed', reason: job.error ?? 'remote job failed' };
    return { status: 'running' };
  })
  .poll('10m');

const score = H.command('score-eval')
  .input(z.object({ resultsUri: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ score: z.number(), breakdown: z.record(z.string(), z.number()) }))
  .runner(workstation)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (i, ctx) =>
    z.object({ score: z.number(), breakdown: z.record(z.string(), z.number()) }).parse(JSON.parse((await ctx.sh(`./score.sh ${i.resultsUri}`)).stdout)),
  );

  .input(z.object({ checkpoint: z.string(), score: z.number(), breakdown: z.record(z.string(), z.number()) }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt((i) => `Checkpoint ${i.checkpoint} scored ${i.score}. Breakdown: ${JSON.stringify(i.breakdown)}`);

const evaluate = H.flow('evaluate')
  .input(evalSchema)
  .step('prepare', prepare)
  .step('gpu', gpuEvaluation, (s) => ({ evalId: s.input.evalId, bundle: s.steps.prepare.bundle }))
  .step('score', score, (s) => ({ resultsUri: s.steps.gpu.resultsUri }))
  .step('summarize', analyst.call(summarizeEval), (s) => ({

  }))

const evalRuns = H.lane('eval-runs')
  .of(evalRunKind)
  .from(supply.manual())
  .store(store)

const migrationSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), database: databaseName, sql: z.string() });
const migrationKind = H.work('Migration').schema(migrationSchema).states(queued, working, finished, failed, parked, cancelled);

const applyMigration = H.command('apply-migration')
  .input(migrationSchema)
  .runner(databaseRunner)
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(`psql "$${urlVariable[i.database]}" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction`, { stdin: i.sql });
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
  });

const migrate = H.flow('migrate')
  .input(migrationSchema)

  .step('apply', applyMigration)
  .exit('applied');

const previousMigration = (id: string) => {
  const number = Number.parseInt(id, 10);
  return number > 1 ? String(number - 1).padStart(id.length, '0') : undefined;
};

const migrations = H.lane('migrations')
  .of(migrationKind)
  .from(supply.folder({ path: 'migrations', schema: migrationSchema }).key((d) => d.id))
  .store(store)
  .handle(migrate)
  .exits({ applied: finished })
  .retry({ tries: 0, backoff: 'none', exhausted: failed })
  .after((d) => previousMigration(d.id), { failed: parked });

const backfillSchema = z.object({ table: z.string(), database: databaseName, transform: z.string() });
const backfillKind = H.work('Backfill').schema(backfillSchema).states(queued, working, finished, failed, cancelled);
const batchRows = 10_000;

const copyBatch = H.command('backfill-batch')
  .input(z.object({ table: z.string(), database: databaseName, transform: z.string(), offset: z.number(), limit: z.number() }))
  .output(z.object({ rows: z.number() }))
  .runner(databaseRunner)
  .effect('repeatable')
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(
      `./backfill.sh "$${urlVariable[i.database]}" ${i.table} ${i.transform} --offset ${i.offset} --limit ${i.limit}`,
    );
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
    return { rows: Number.parseInt(result.stdout.trim(), 10) };
  });

const backfill = H.flow('backfill')
  .input(backfillSchema)
  .resources((s) => [H.lease.shared(databases[s.input.database])])
  .loop('batches', {
    maxIterations: 100_000,
    initial: () => 0,
    body: (batch) =>
      batch.step('copy', copyBatch, (s) => ({
        table: s.input.table,
        database: s.input.database,
        transform: s.input.transform,
        offset: s.carry,
        limit: batchRows,
      })),
    next: (s) => s.carry + s.steps.copy.rows,
    until: (s) => s.steps.copy.rows < batchRows,
  })
  .exit((s) => (s.steps.batches.completed ? 'backfilled' : 'tooManyBatches'));

const backfills = H.lane('backfills')
  .of(backfillKind)
  .from(supply.manual())
  .store(store)
  .handle(backfill)
  .exits({ backfilled: finished, tooManyBatches: failed })
  .retry({ tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: failed });

const gpuJobSeconds = H.metric('gpu-job-seconds').sum(H.events.jobs(), 'durationSeconds');
const leaseWaitSeconds = H.metric('lease-wait-seconds').median(H.events.leases(), 'waitSeconds');

export const mlPlatform = H.harness('ml-platform')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.sqlite'))
  .pools(apiPool)
  .lanes(evalRuns, migrations, backfills)
  .scheduler(H.scheduler().policy(H.policy.schedule('oldest-first', ({ candidates }) => [...candidates].sort((a, b) => b.waitingSeconds - a.waitingSeconds))))
  .grants(
    H.grant(http.client('operator', { port: 8720, token: H.env('OPERATOR_TOKEN') }), H.ops.work.read, H.ops.work.write, H.ops.telemetry.read),
    H.grant(claudeCode.client('platform-supervisor', { session: 'platform' }), H.ops.work.read, H.ops.work.write, H.ops.telemetry.read),
  )
  .metrics(gpuJobSeconds, leaseWaitSeconds)
  .observe(observers.board({ path: '.harness/board.md' }), observers.telemetry({ path: '.harness/telemetry.md' }));

=== END ===

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface. A step is a command, a model call, a batch of model calls, or an external job (submitted now, collected later by a poll or a callback: a cloud batch, a GPU run, a long service call); a batch and an external job hold no capacity while they run. (External jobs ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role, resource, halt). A resource (a file pattern, a database, a section, a host) is a named shared thing that leases, memory scope and metric facets reference by identity; a string never stands in for it. A halt is a named question with a decision schema that grants, metrics, timers and policies reference by identity. *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall, seat = role × models × choice policy: a seat holds a role with the model a deterministic policy picks at attempt time, an agent is a seat with one model, and metrics on an A/B comparison key on the seat so a model swap does not break the series). (Resources, halts and seats ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts. By default a failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy, and the lane's policy names where exhaustion leaves the unit, in the kind's own states; the kind declares nothing about failure. Where an active unit stands in its work is its attempt's current step, read from the ledger; a kind declares no states for it, and waiting on a human is the attempt's blocked state, recorded once. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why. The failure default was added after generation 1, when three of eleven children read the silence as "every kind declares a failure state" and invented states that loop or dead-end. Retry's end state moved to the lane, and the active position was ruled, on 2026-11-01 after run one: three generation-3 adversaries showed a move on the kind only means something given the lane's policy, and three generations modelled waiting on a human twice.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable, and it may be partitioned by backend. Account quota shared by several harnesses is a ledger partition of append-only quota events: each harness appends its own consumption and folds the window at read time, so no harness takes a lock over another's account state. The account names its quota partition, as every instance carries its backend; the ledger carries no option for it. A quota store that needs the ledger's single-writer lock, or a second store under the ledger's name, breaks this principle. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all. (Shared quota ruled 2026-11-01 after generation 1.)
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted; a grant names the halt it may resolve. A halt's resolver is a human, a registered policy (a deterministic function whose decision is recorded with the metrics and sample counts it read), or a clock: a timeout default that resolves the halt without cancelling the attempt. Deadlines on a halt run from the recorded halt, never from unit data. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished". A metric dimension is a typed ledger column (kind, lane, state, model, seat, resource, halt) or a declared facet entity; a facet that repeats a column is a startup error. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.
