declare module 'harness-dsl' {
  import { z } from 'zod';
  import {
    Named,
    EnvRef,
    PortRef,
    Verdict,
    Position,
    State,
    UnitView,
    WorkRef,
    Metrics,
    Policy,
    AccountState,
    Account,
    Model,
    RunnerBackend,
    Workspace,
    Supplier,
    Store,
    MemoryStore,
    Ledger,
    Client,
    Observer,
    Scope,
    MetricRef,
    Measure,
    Window,
    ResolvedBy,
    Dims,
    FacetValue,
    FacetRef,
    HaltRef,
    RoleRef,
    SeatRef,
    Resource,
    ColumnName,
  } from 'harness-dsl/kernel';
  export * from 'harness-dsl/kernel';

  export type Schema<T> = z.ZodType<T>;
  export type Empty = { readonly [K in never]: never };
  export type StepOf<St> = Extract<keyof St, string>;

  export interface KindShape<A, S extends State> extends WorkRef<S['name']> {
    readonly entity: 'kind';
    readonly _types?: { readonly attrs: A; readonly states: S };
  }

  export interface Kind<N extends string, A, S extends State> extends KindShape<A, S> {
    readonly name: N;
    attributes<A2 extends object>(schema: Schema<A2>): Kind<N, A2, S>;
    states<S2 extends State[]>(...states: S2): Kind<N, A, S2[number]>;
    key(identity: (attrs: A) => string): Kind<N, A, S>;
    initial(state: S): Kind<N, A, S>;
  }

  export interface Signal<N extends string = string, P = unknown> extends Named {
    readonly entity: 'signal';
    readonly name: N;
    readonly _payload?: P;
    payload<P2>(schema: Schema<P2>): Signal<N, P2>;
  }

  export interface Halt<N extends string = string, D = unknown> extends HaltRef {
    readonly name: N;
    readonly _decision?: D;
    decision<D2>(schema: Schema<D2>): Halt<N, D2>;
  }

  export interface Facet<N extends string = string> extends FacetRef {
    readonly name: N;
    of(value: string): FacetValue;
    read(by: Dims): string | undefined;
  }

  export interface Executable<I, O> extends Named {
    readonly _io?: { readonly in: (input: I) => void; readonly out: O };
  }

  export interface Batch<I, O> extends Executable<readonly I[], readonly O[]> {
    readonly submission: 'batch';
  }

  export interface CommandResult {
    readonly exitCode: number;
    readonly stdout: string;
    readonly stderr: string;
  }

  export interface Command<I, O> extends Executable<I, O> {
    input<I2>(schema: Schema<I2>): Command<I2, O>;
    argv(argv: readonly string[] | ((input: I) => readonly string[])): Command<I, O>;
    output<O2>(schema: Schema<O2>): Command<I, O2>;
    runner(runner: Runner | ((input: I) => Runner)): Command<I, O>;
    acceptExitCodes(...exitCodes: number[]): Command<I, O>;
  }

  export interface Runner extends Named {
    readonly backend: RunnerBackend;
    slots(count: number): Runner;
    preflight(check: Executable<void, unknown>): Runner;
  }

  export type Intent = 'read' | 'edit' | 'run' | 'search' | 'browse' | 'record';

  export interface Role extends RoleRef {
    intents(...intents: Intent[]): Role;
    instructions(text: string): Role;
  }

  export interface Task {
    readonly task: string;
    readonly resources?: readonly Resource[];
    readonly skills?: readonly string[];
  }

  export interface PolicyCtx {
    readonly kind: WorkRef;
    readonly seat: SeatRef;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
  }

  export interface ModelPolicy extends Policy<PolicyCtx, Model> {
    readonly candidates: readonly Model[];
  }

  export interface Seat<O> extends Executable<Task, O>, SeatRef {
    role(role: Role): Seat<O>;
    model(model: Model | ModelPolicy): Seat<O>;
    pool(pool: Pool): Seat<O>;
    output<O2>(schema: Schema<O2>): Seat<O2>;
    workspace(workspace: Workspace): Seat<O>;
    guard(guard: { readonly leaseFiles?: boolean; readonly beforeStop?: Executable<void, unknown> }): Seat<O>;
    halts(...halts: Halt<string, unknown>[]): Seat<O>;
    batch(): Batch<Task, O>;
  }

  export interface AccountPolicyCtx {
    readonly candidates: readonly AccountState[];
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export type AccountPolicy = Policy<AccountPolicyCtx, AccountState | undefined>;

  export interface HaltPolicyCtx<I> {
    readonly input: I;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
  }

  export interface HaltPolicy<I, D> extends Policy<HaltPolicyCtx<I>, D | undefined> {
    readonly halt: HaltRef;
    readonly _input?: I;
  }

  export interface Pool extends Named {
    accounts(...accounts: Account[]): Pool;
    share(account: Account, fraction: number): Pool;
    drain(policy: AccountPolicy): Pool;
    fallback(account: Account): Pool;
  }

  export interface MemoryKind extends Named {
    readonly entity: 'memoryKind';
    readonly trust: 'experience' | 'taste';
  }

  export interface Journal extends Named {
    readonly entity: 'journal';
    store(store: MemoryStore): Journal;
    recall(recall: { readonly by: 'specificity' | 'similarity'; readonly limit: number }): Journal;
    readBy(...roles: Role[]): Journal;
    recordedBy(...roles: Role[]): Journal;
  }

  export interface MemoryDraft {
    readonly text: string;
    readonly when?: Scope;
    readonly status?: 'candidate' | 'active';
  }

  export interface Retry {
    readonly maxAttempts: number;
    readonly backoff: 'fixed' | 'exponential';
    readonly initialDelayMs: number;
  }

  export interface StepOptions<I> {
    readonly retry?: Retry;
    readonly afterCrash?: 'rerun' | 'park' | 'askDriver';
    readonly alreadyDone?: Executable<I, boolean>;
  }

  export interface FlowCtx<In, P, St> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<In>;
    readonly params: P;
    readonly steps: St;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
    readonly now: Date;
    readonly iteration: number;
  }

  export interface ChildResult {
    readonly unitId: string;
    readonly state: string;
    readonly verdict: Verdict;
  }

  export interface JobHandle {
    readonly jobId: string;
  }

  export interface JobPoll<O> {
    readonly state: 'running' | 'succeeded' | 'failed';
    readonly result?: O;
    readonly reason?: string;
  }

  export interface HaltOptions<In, P, St, D, I> {
    readonly ask: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => string;
    readonly askIf?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => boolean;
    readonly skip?: { readonly by: HaltPolicy<I, D>; readonly input: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => I };
    readonly timeout?: { readonly afterMinutes: number; readonly decide: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => D };
    readonly escalate?: { readonly afterMinutes: number; readonly run: Executable<void, unknown> };
  }

  export interface Flow<In, P, St, X extends string, N extends string, B extends string> extends Named {
    readonly _types?: {
      readonly input: (attrs: In) => void;
      readonly params: (params: P) => P;
      readonly steps: St;
      readonly exits: X;
      readonly runningSteps: N;
      readonly blockingSteps: B;
    };
    input<In2>(schema: Schema<In2>): Flow<In2, P, St, X, N, B>;
    params<P2>(schema: Schema<P2>): Flow<In, P2, St, X, N, B>;
    step<M extends string, I, O>(
      name: M,
      exec: Batch<I, O>,
      input: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => readonly I[],
      options?: StepOptions<readonly I[]>,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: readonly O[] }, X, N, B | M>;
    step<M extends string, O>(
      name: M,
      exec: Executable<void, O>,
      options?: StepOptions<void>,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: O }, X, N | M, B>;
    step<M extends string, I, O>(
      name: M,
      exec: Executable<I, O>,
      input: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => I,
      options?: StepOptions<I>,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: O }, X, N | M, B>;
    halt<M extends string, D, I = never>(
      name: M,
      halt: Halt<string, D>,
      options: HaltOptions<In, P, St, NoInfer<D>, I> & { readonly askIf: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => boolean },
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: D | undefined }, X, N, B | M>;
    halt<M extends string, D, I = never>(
      name: M,
      halt: Halt<string, D>,
      options: HaltOptions<In, P, St, NoInfer<D>, I>,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: D }, X, N, B | M>;
    wait<M extends string>(
      name: M,
      wait: { readonly ms: number },
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: Date }, X, N, B | M>;
    job<M extends string, I, O>(
      name: M,
      job: {
        readonly submit: Executable<I, JobHandle>;
        readonly input: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => I;
        readonly collect: Executable<JobHandle, JobPoll<O>>;
        readonly pollEveryMinutes: number;
      },
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: O }, X, N, B | M>;
    spawn<M extends string, A2>(
      name: M,
      lane: LaneShape<A2, State, unknown>,
      children: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => readonly A2[],
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: readonly ChildResult[] }, X, N, B | M>;
    loop<M extends string, St2, X2 extends string, N2 extends string, B2 extends string>(
      name: M,
      body: (flow: Flow<In, P, St, X, N, B>) => Flow<In, P, St2, X2, N2, B2>,
      bounds: {
        readonly max?: number | ((ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => number);
        readonly until?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St2>) => boolean;
      },
    ): Flow<In, P, St2, X2, N2, B2>;
    exit<M extends string>(
      name: M,
      when?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => boolean,
    ): Flow<In, P, St, X | M, N, B>;
  }

  export interface LaneShape<A, S extends State, St> extends WorkRef<S['name']> {
    readonly entity: 'lane';
    readonly _types?: { readonly attrs: A; readonly states: S; readonly steps: St };
  }

  export type LaneRef = LaneShape<unknown, State, unknown>;

  export type ActiveState<S extends State> = Extract<S, State<string, 'active'>>;
  export type WaitingState<S extends State> = Extract<S, State<string, 'waiting'>>;

  export interface HandlerMap<S extends State, X extends string, N extends string, B extends string> {
    readonly exits: { readonly [K in X]: S };
    readonly during?: { readonly [K in N]?: ActiveState<S> } & { readonly [K in B]?: WaitingState<S> };
  }

  export type InputFits<A, I> = [A] extends [I] ? unknown : { readonly flowInputDoesNotFitKind: I };

  export interface Reaction<A, S extends State, N extends string, P> {
    readonly update?: (attrs: A, payload: P) => A;
    readonly restart?: N | { readonly to: N; readonly at: readonly N[] };
    readonly enter?: S;
  }

  export interface Route { readonly route: 'create' | 'signal' | 'skip' }

  export interface Router<A, SN extends string, StepN extends string = string> {
    create(attrs: A): Route;
    signal<P>(
      signal: Signal<string, P>,
      target: string | ((unit: UnitView<A, SN, StepN>) => boolean),
      payload: P,
    ): Route;
    skip(): Route;
  }

  export interface OperatorSupplier extends Named { readonly operator: true }

  export interface Lease {
    readonly resource: Resource;
    readonly mode: 'exclusive' | 'shared';
  }

  export interface Lane<A, S extends State, St, N extends string> extends LaneShape<A, S, St> {
    readonly _types?: { readonly attrs: A; readonly states: S; readonly steps: St; readonly stepNames: N };
    supply(supplier: OperatorSupplier): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    supply<E>(
      supplier: Supplier<E>,
      route: (event: E, to: Router<A, S['name'], N>) => Route | readonly Route[],
    ): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    store(store: Store): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    store<M extends string>(store: Store<M>, states: { readonly [K in S['name']]: M }): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    handler<I, St2, X extends string, N2 extends string, B2 extends string>(
      flow: Flow<I, void, St2, X, N2, B2>,
      map: HandlerMap<S, X, N2, B2> & InputFits<A, I>,
    ): Lane<A, S, St2, N2 | B2>;
    handler<I, P, St2, X extends string, N2 extends string, B2 extends string>(
      flow: Flow<I, P, St2, X, N2, B2>,
      map: HandlerMap<S, X, N2, B2> & { readonly params: P } & InputFits<A, I>,
    ): Lane<A, S, St2, N2 | B2>;
    retry(retry: Retry & { readonly exhausted: S }): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    lease(pick: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name'], N>) => Lease): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    after(order: {
      readonly key: (attrs: A) => string | undefined;
      readonly onPredecessorFailed: WaitingState<S>;
    }): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    on<P>(signal: Signal<string, P>, reaction: Reaction<A, S, N, P>): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    ceiling(ceiling: {
      readonly maxUsd: number;
      readonly onExceed: 'fail' | Halt<string, CeilingDecision>;
    }): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
  }

  export type CeilingDecision =
    | { readonly action: 'raise'; readonly maxUsd: number }
    | { readonly action: 'fail' };

  export interface Tick { readonly at: Date }
  export type Weekday = 'mon' | 'tue' | 'wed' | 'thu' | 'fri' | 'sat' | 'sun';

  export interface Clock extends Supplier<Tick> {
    every(interval: { readonly minutes: number }): Clock;
    at(time: string, options?: { readonly on?: Weekday | number; readonly tz?: string }): Clock;
  }

  export interface Invoked {
    readonly seat?: SeatRef;
    readonly model?: Model;
  }

  export interface TransitionEvent<A, SN extends string = string, StepN extends string = string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN, StepN>;
    readonly to: SN;
    readonly attempt?: { readonly durationMs: number; readonly costUsd: number };
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface PatternEvent<A, SN extends string = string, StepN extends string = string>
    extends TransitionEvent<A, SN, StepN> {
    readonly group: string;
    readonly streak: number;
  }

  export interface TimerEvent<A, SN extends string = string, StepN extends string = string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN, StepN>;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface StepEvent<A, O, St, SN extends string = string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN, StepOf<St>>;
    readonly ok: boolean;
    readonly output?: O;
    readonly outputs: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: St[K] };
    readonly invocations: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: Invoked };
    readonly durationMs: number;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface DecisionEvent<A, D, St, SN extends string = string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN, StepOf<St>>;
    readonly decision: D;
    readonly resolvedBy: ResolvedBy;
    readonly resolver: string;
    readonly waitedMs: number;
    readonly outputs: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: St[K] };
    readonly invocations: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: Invoked };
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface InvocationEvent {
    readonly seat?: SeatRef;
    readonly model?: Model;
    readonly ok: boolean;
    readonly costUsd: number;
  }

  export type Threshold = { readonly below: number } | { readonly above: number };

  export interface Band {
    readonly window: Window;
    readonly minSamples: number;
    readonly enter: Threshold;
    readonly exit: Threshold;
  }

  export interface CrossingEvent {
    readonly by: Dims;
    readonly value: number;
    readonly samples: number;
  }

  export interface Source<E> extends Named { readonly _event?: E }

  export type StateMatch<S extends State> = S | readonly S[];

  export interface TriggerRef extends Named {
    readonly entity: 'trigger';
  }

  export interface Trigger<E> extends TriggerRef {
    on<E2>(source: Source<E2>): Trigger<E2>;
    create<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, attrs: (event: E) => A | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    signal<P>(
      signal: Signal<string, P>,
      lane: LaneRef,
      target: (event: E) => { readonly key: string; readonly payload: P } | undefined,
    ): Trigger<E>;
    record(journal: Journal, item: (event: E) => MemoryDraft | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    pause(lane: LaneRef, reason: (event: E) => string): Trigger<E>;
    resume(lane: LaneRef, reason: (event: E) => string): Trigger<E>;
  }

  export interface Sample { readonly hit: boolean; readonly by?: Dims }
  export interface Amount { readonly amount: number; readonly by?: Dims }

  export interface MetricDraft<E> extends Named {
    facets(...facets: Facet[]): MetricDraft<E>;
    samples(extract: (event: E) => readonly Sample[]): MetricRef<'rate'>;
    amounts(extract: (event: E) => readonly Amount[]): MetricRef<'total'>;
  }

  export interface AdmitCtx<A> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A>;
    readonly count: (lane: LaneRef, ...positions: Position[]) => number;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
  }

  export interface Scheduler extends Named {
    priority(...lanes: LaneRef[]): Scheduler;
    wip(lane: LaneRef, maxActive: number): Scheduler;
    boost(lane: LaneRef, aging: { readonly afterMinutes: number }): Scheduler;
    rank<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, key: (unit: UnitView<A>) => number): Scheduler;
    admit<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, gate: (ctx: AdmitCtx<A>) => boolean): Scheduler;
  }

  export interface Operation<I, O> extends Named {
    readonly _io?: { readonly in: (input: I) => void; readonly out: O };
  }

  export type Grant = Operation<never, unknown>;

  export interface Harness extends Named {
    ledger(ledger: Ledger): Harness;
    lanes(...lanes: LaneRef[]): Harness;
    journals(...journals: Journal[]): Harness;
    triggers(...triggers: TriggerRef[]): Harness;
    metrics(...metrics: MetricRef<Measure>[]): Harness;
    scheduler(scheduler: Scheduler): Harness;
    clients(...clients: Client[]): Harness;
    observers(...observers: Observer[]): Harness;
    start(): Promise<void>;
  }

  export const H: {
    env(name: string): EnvRef;
    readonly slot: { port(slot: number): PortRef };
    nextTime(at: string, options: { readonly after: Date; readonly tz?: string }): Date;

    kind<N extends string>(name: N): Kind<N, Empty, never>;
    state<N extends string, P extends 'pending' | 'active' | 'waiting'>(name: N, position: P): State<N, P>;
    terminal<N extends string>(name: N, verdict: Verdict): State<N, 'terminal'>;
    signal<N extends string>(name: N): Signal<N, Empty>;
    halt<N extends string>(name: N): Halt<N, Empty>;
    resource(name: string): Resource;
    facet<N extends string>(name: N & (N extends ColumnName ? never : unknown)): Facet<N>;
    readonly cancel: Signal<'cancel', { readonly reason?: string }>;
    role(name: string): Role;
    memory(name: string, trust: 'experience' | 'taste'): MemoryKind;

    command(name: string): Command<void, CommandResult>;
    jobPoll<O>(result: Schema<O>): Schema<JobPoll<O>>;
    seat(name: string): Seat<string>;
    pool(name: string): Pool;
    readonly policy: {
      model(name: string, candidates: readonly Model[], choose: (ctx: PolicyCtx) => Model): ModelPolicy;
      account(name: string, choose: (ctx: AccountPolicyCtx) => AccountState | undefined): AccountPolicy;
      halt<I, D>(
        name: string,
        halt: Halt<string, D>,
        input: Schema<I>,
        decide: (ctx: HaltPolicyCtx<I>) => NoInfer<D> | undefined,
      ): HaltPolicy<I, D>;
    };

    flow(name: string): Flow<unknown, void, Empty, never, never, never>;
    lane<A, S extends State>(name: string, kind: KindShape<A, S>): Lane<A, S, Empty, never>;
    journal(name: string, of: MemoryKind): Journal;
    clock(name: string): Clock;
    readonly operator: OperatorSupplier;

    trigger(name: string): Trigger<never>;
    readonly when: {
      transition<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        filter?: {
          readonly to?: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly if?: (event: TransitionEvent<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>) => boolean;
        },
      ): Source<TransitionEvent<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>>;
      pattern<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        pattern: {
          readonly to: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly consecutive: number;
          readonly per: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>) => string;
        },
      ): Source<PatternEvent<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>>;
      timer<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        timer: { readonly at: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>) => Date | undefined },
      ): Source<TimerEvent<A, S['name'], StepOf<St>>>;
      step<A, S extends State, St, M extends StepOf<St>>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        step: M,
        filter?: { readonly if?: (event: StepEvent<A, St[M], St, S['name']>) => boolean },
      ): Source<StepEvent<A, St[M], St, S['name']>>;
      decision<A, S extends State, St, D>(
        lanes: LaneShape<A, S, St> | readonly LaneShape<A, S, St>[],
        halt: Halt<string, D>,
      ): Source<DecisionEvent<A, D, St, S['name']>>;
      invocation(filter: { readonly lanes: readonly LaneRef[] }): Source<InvocationEvent>;
      crossing(
        metric: MetricRef<'rate'>,
        band: Band,
        edge: 'entered' | 'exited',
      ): Source<CrossingEvent>;
    };
    metric<E>(name: string, source: Source<E>): MetricDraft<E>;
    scheduler(name: string): Scheduler;

    operation<O>(name: string, exec: Executable<void, O>): Operation<void, O>;
    readonly ops: {
      readonly workRead: Grant;
      readonly workCreate: Grant;
      readonly workUpdate: Grant;
      readonly workCancel: Grant;
      readonly workSignal: Grant;
      readonly attemptsRecover: Grant;
      readonly lanesPause: Grant;
      readonly memoryRead: Grant;
      readonly memoryWrite: Grant;
      readonly memoryCurate: Grant;
      readonly telemetryRead: Grant;
      readonly accountsRead: Grant;
      readonly accountsShare: Grant;
      resolve(halt: HaltRef): Grant;
    };
    harness(name: string): Harness;
  };
}

  .runner(runner);

  .input(negotiationTerms)
  .step('draft', negotiator, ctx => ({
    task: `Negotiate ${ctx.unit.attributes.item} with ${ctx.unit.attributes.vendor}, ceiling ${ctx.unit.attributes.ceilingUsd} USD. Vendor last offered ${ctx.unit.attributes.lastVendorOffer ?? 'nothing'}: ${ctx.unit.attributes.lastVendorMessage ?? ''}`,
  }))
  .step('send', sendToVendor, ctx => ({ negotiationId: ctx.unit.attributes.negotiationId, message: ctx.steps.draft.message }), {
    afterCrash: 'park',
    alreadyDone: vendorMessageDelivered,
  })
  .exit('agreed', ctx => ctx.steps.draft.action === 'accept')
  .exit('walkedAway', ctx => ctx.steps.draft.action === 'walkAway')
  .exit('offered');

const vendorReplies = webhook.json('vendor-replies', {
  port: H.slot.port(2),
  path: '/vendor',
  secret: H.env('VENDOR_SECRET'),
  payload: z.object({
    negotiationId: z.string(),
    reply: z.enum(['counter', 'accept', 'walkAway']),
    offerUsd: z.number(),
    message: z.string(),
  }),

  .supply(H.operator)
  .supply(vendorReplies, (r, to) => {

        return to.signal(vendorCountered, r.negotiationId, { offerUsd: r.offerUsd, message: r.message });
      case 'accept':

  .on(vendorCountered, {

  .on(vendorAccepted, { update: (a, p) => ({ ...a, lastVendorOffer: p.offerUsd }), enter: Agreed })
  .on(vendorWalkedAway, { update: (a, p) => ({ ...a, lastVendorMessage: p.message }), enter: TheyWalkedAway })

  .wip(tenancies, 3)
  .wip(negotiations, 2)

# harness-dsl: ours-2, net-shaped execution

This child keeps the owner's vocabulary: unit, attempt, step, state, lane, halt, trigger. It reads the execution model as a Petri net:

- states are **places**;
- units are **tokens**;
- attempts, moves and retries are **transitions**;
- WIP, runner slots and leases are **capacity places**.

Only one lens word enters the surface: **marking**, the count of tokens per lane and position that the scheduler reads. Everything else the lens gives is semantics, written down below.

## Entities

### Kinds (pure vocabulary, no backend)

| Builder | Produces |
|---|---|
| `H.work(name).schema(z).states(...)` | A work kind: its data shape and its places. |
| `H.state(name).pending() / .active() / .waiting() / .terminal(verdict)` | A place with its skeleton position. A terminal place carries `success`, `failure` or `neutral`, with no default. |
| `H.resource(name)` | A named shared thing. It is a capacity place for leases, and an identity for memory scope and metrics. |
| `H.halt(name).context(z).ask(...).decision(z)` | A named question. A flow places it at one or more addresses. |
| `H.memory(name).content(z).trust(...)` | A memory kind. The kernel owns the envelope. |
| `H.role(name)` | A prompt, intents, recall and record kinds, and plugins. |
| `H.skill(name)` | A typed contract for one model call. |
| `H.facet(name)` | A metric dimension that is not a ledger column. |

### Instances (carry a backend)

| Builder | Notes |
|---|---|
| `H.account`, `H.model` | As in the parent. |
| `H.runner.local / ssh` | A capacity place of `slots` tokens. |
| `H.command(name)` | A deterministic executable. `.effect('repeatable' \| 'unrepeatable')` sets its restart behaviour, and `.detect` probes whether it already ran. `.runner(r)` is the default runner. |
| `H.job(name)` | Submit, then collect by poll. |

### Pivots (each has a noun)

| Pivot | Connects | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| **pool** | accounts × policy × models served | the account for one invocation |
| **seat** `H.seat(name).role(r).models(...).policy(p?)` | role × models × choice policy | the model for one attempt. A seat with one model is what the brief calls an agent. |
| **lane** `H.lane(name).of(kind).from(...).store(s).handle(flow, arcs)` plus `wip`, `ceiling`, `after`, `facet`, `deadline` | kind × suppliers × store × handler | the lane's units and attempts |
| **journal** | memory kind × store × recall | recalled items |
| **grant** | client × operations | a client's rights |
| **trigger** `H.trigger(name).on(source).when(p).do(...)` | recorded source × consequences | recorded firings |
| **flow** | executables, halts, forks | the handler |

**Executables.** Every executable implements `Executable<I, O>`. There are four:

- a `Command`;
- a `Job`;
- a `Call`, made by `seat.call(skill)`;
- a `Batch`, made by `seat.batch(skill)`. A batch is a job whose submit and collect belong to the account driver. It is a step like any other, not a flow method.

**Sources** are top-level builders:

- `H.entered(lane, ...states)`
- `H.streak(lane, state, n, { by })`
- `H.due(lane)`
- `H.opened(halt)`, with `.after(d)` or `.at(fn)`
- `H.resolved(halt)`
- `H.crossing(metric, opts)`, with `.falls()` and `.rises()`

**Consequences** are top-level builders too:

- `H.create(lane, map, { key })`
- `H.move(lane, state, key?)`
- `H.pause(lane)` and `H.resume(lane)`
- `H.record(journal, map)`
- `H.run(command, map)`
- `H.resolve(halt, decide | policy)`

A lane is no longer a source or a consequence.

**Policies** have six constructors: `H.policy.pool`, `.seat`, `.schedule`, `.recall`, `.halt` and `.runner`. Every one is deterministic, and every metric it reads is recorded on `policy.decided` with its value and sample count.

### Words

- **run**: one process lifetime under one ledger claim.
- **attempt**: one firing of a lane's handler for a unit. Its outcome is succeeded, failed or cancelled.
- **step**: one addressed node of a flow (`flow/path`, plus the flow hash).
- **invocation**: one model call.
- **marking**: the scheduler's read-only view of how many units each lane holds at each position.

## Execution model (the net)

1. **Unit marking.** Each unit is one token in one of its kind's places. Its position is the place's position, with one refinement: an attempt whose every branch token sits at a waiting address (a halt, a job, a batch or a spawn) shows the unit at `waiting`.
2. **Attempt start** is a transition from a pending place to the kind's active place. It is enabled when all of these hold:
   - the lane is not paused;
   - the lane's WIP place has a free token;
   - every lease the flow selects is available. An exclusive lease takes the whole resource place; a shared lease takes one token and is inhibited by an exclusive holder;
   - every `after` predecessor is terminal at a success verdict;
   - the schedule policy ordered the unit this tick.
3. **Inside an attempt** the flow is a sub-net.
   - Each step is a transition that consumes a runner slot while it runs.
   - `parallel(name, { a, b })` forks one token per branch and joins when all branches complete. The fork and the join are recorded (`branch.forked`, `branch.joined`), and branch addresses are `name/branch/step`.
   - A token at a waiting address holds no runner slot and no WIP. When the address completes (a halt is resolved, a job is collected, the children of a spawn are terminal), the attempt becomes a `resuming` candidate. To continue, it takes a WIP token through the schedule policy, like any start.
4. **Attempt end** is a transition from the active place along an arc of the lane's `handle(flow, { exits, retry, input? })`:
   - an exit label leads to a place, or to a bound `{ to, maxTimes, then }`, which the kernel counts per unit;
   - a failure returns the unit to the pending place it started from, under `retry`;
   - exhaustion leads to `retry.exhausted`.

   Exits and retry are the arcs of one handler, so they now live in one argument and are typed against the flow's labels.
5. **External transitions.**
   - `H.move(lane, state, key?)` withdraws every token of the open attempt. The attempt is cancelled and the running step's signal is aborted. The unit moves to the place, and the move is recorded.
   - Operator moves are the same transition, made through `H.ops.work.write`.
6. **Signals.** A supplier offer whose key matches a non-terminal unit updates that unit. What happens next depends on where the attempt's tokens are:
   - If any branch token is running, the update is deferred to the next attempt. It is recorded and not lost.
   - If every token waits at a halt, the attempt is cancelled (`interrupted`) and the unit returns to pending, so the next attempt starts from the top.
   - If the unit sits in a waiting place, it returns to pending.
7. **Keys and deduplication.** A key names at most one non-terminal unit per lane.
   - `H.create` with a key that is open records `unit.deduplicated` and creates nothing.
   - Once that unit is terminal, the key may be reused: the next create, or the next supplier offer, makes a new unit with a new id.
   - This is scenario 9's "one Audit per category while open", and scenario 3's weekly re-opening of a reported Topic.
8. **Time.**
   - `lane.deadline(fn)` arms one timer per unit. The timer re-arms on every recorded update, so an extended SLA disarms the old deadline; both `timer.disarmed` and `timer.armed` are recorded. A deadline function that returns `undefined` disarms the timer.
   - `H.due(lane)` fires on the timer.
   - Halt clocks run from the recorded `halt.opened`.
   - A schedule candidate carries its `deadline`, so ordering by time to breach needs no unit-data access.
9. **Pause.**
   - `H.pause(lane)` puts an inhibitor on the lane's start transition. Running attempts finish.
   - The `lane.paused` event records the firing trigger and its source payload. When the payload is a crossing, its `value` and `samples` become the board's `PauseView`. There is no free-text reason.

## Rules

- **Scheduler.** `harness.schedule(policy)` (`H.scheduler()` is removed). The policy receives:
  - `candidates`, each with its unit, the lane descriptor itself (compare by identity), the waiting time, the deadline and the `resuming` flag;
  - `running`, the current attempts;
  - `marking`, with `count(lane, ...positions)` and `paused(lane)`.

  It returns an ordered subset. "No new Backup while an Incident is active" reads `marking.count(incidents, 'active', 'waiting') > 0`.
- **Runner choice.** A step's runner may be a `RunnerPolicy` from `H.policy.runner(name, runners, decide)`.
  - It receives the typed flow state and each candidate runner with its free slots.
  - It returns runners in order of preference. The chosen runner is recorded with the decision.
  - One flow and one lane therefore serve two backup hosts.
- **Metrics.**
  - Columns are exactly principle 18's: `kind`, `lane`, `state`, `model`, `seat`, `resource` and `halt`. The resolver sort is a filter on `decisions`, not a column.
  - `where.seat` / `where.model` select events whose own column matches, or whose attempt invoked that seat on that model.
  - `H.events.steps(flow, step)` takes the flow entity and a step name typed from that flow's steps, so a renamed step is a compile error.
  - `H.events.credits(halt, d => seats)` emits one event per seat a decision credits, with the `seat` column set. It is how scenario 6 keys "acted on" by seat.
- **Halts.**
  - The three resolver sorts are human, policy and clock, as in the parent.
  - Two halts may be open at once in parallel branches. Each has its own address, its own clock and its own grant.
- **Resumption.** Replay over the memoizing ledger, as in the parent.
  - Completed addresses return their recorded output.
  - The address that was started at the crash follows its effect:
    - a `repeatable` command reruns;
    - an `unrepeatable` command calls `detect`, and otherwise blocks the attempt (`interrupted`);
    - a `Call` asks its driver to `recover`;
    - a `Job` or `Batch` with a recorded ref is collected;
    - a halt reads its resolution;
    - a spawn reads its children.
  - Fork and join records restore every branch token.
  - A flow-hash mismatch blocks the attempt (`definitionChanged`).
  - Ledger claims are exclusive and taken over only from a stale holder.
  - The author writes nothing for any of this.
- **Quota.** Accounts name a `QuotaPartition`. Consumption is append-only and folded at read time.
- **Startup validation.** `start()` rejects all of the following:
  - duplicate names within an entity sort;
  - an exit label or retry target outside the lane's kind;
  - a kind with two active places, or a terminal place without a verdict;
  - a lane, journal or halt referenced by a trigger, spawn, grant or observer but not registered;
  - a facet named like a column;
  - a seat model no registered pool serves;
  - a recalled memory kind no journal holds;
  - a resource leased or scoped by a flow that no `fileLeaseGuard` maps, when that flow's roles use one;
  - a step address used twice;
  - a `Batch` whose driver lacks `submitBatch`;
  - a runner policy listing a runner whose command runs elsewhere;
  - a `deadline` source on a lane without `deadline`;
  - a `sqlite.reopen` supplier whose path is not the path of the store of the lane it feeds.

## What changed and why

1. **Parallel branches** (`flow.parallel`, the Petri fork and join). The adversary's scenario 13 needs two halts open at once. Branch outputs are typed per branch.
2. **Runner policy** (`H.policy.runner`, step option `runner`). It answers the adversary's critique of scenario 4 (one lane per host) and scenario 13 (a host chosen per attempt).
   - Scenario 4 now has one Backup lane, one flow and one set of triggers.
3. **Marking in the schedule input.** It replaces the opened-minus-closed metric arithmetic that faked preemption.
   - Lane order is by descriptor identity, never by `lane.name`.
4. **Lane split** (critique 3).
   - Sources and consequences move to `H.*` top-level builders.
   - `exits` and `retry` move into `handle(flow, arcs)` as the handler's arcs.
   - `unitOf` is removed: candidates carry `deadline`, and `UnitView.facet(f)` reads facets by entity.
   - The lane keeps 9 methods, down from about 21.
5. **Pause records its cause.** The board's `PauseView` carries the trigger's crossing value and sample count. `pause(reason: string)` is gone.
6. **Key semantics are specified** (rule 7 of the execution model).
7. **`H.agent` is removed** (critique 2, weakness 1). A single-model seat is the agent. There is one noun, one builder, and metrics key on the seat.
8. **Column is trimmed** to principle 18's seven columns. The `external` effect is removed because no scenario used it.
9. **Step metrics address by entity.** They take `H.events.steps(flow, step)` with a typed step name, not a bare string (critique 1).
10. **A/B keys on the seat.** `H.events.credits` attributes editor decisions to seats. The scenario 6 policy reads `where: { seat }`, so a model swap keeps the series.
11. **Batch is a step**, made by `seat.batch(skill)` (weakness 2). This removes `flow.batch`.
12. **`H.scheduler()` is replaced by `harness.schedule(policy)`.** It was an entity with one method.
13. **`lane.deadline` plus `H.due(lane)`** replace `lane.due(fn)`. The deadline is now visible to the scheduler, and its re-arming is recorded.
14. **`sqlite.reopen({ path, cron, schema, where })`** (adapter only, no kernel change). This comes from scenario 3: a weekly schedule re-opens topics tagged `recurring`.
    - A plain `supply.schedule` cannot see which units exist, because its context resolves settings only. The re-opening needs to read the first-party store.
    - The supplier belongs to the store's own adapter, so the kernel `Store` interface stays load/save. It offers each matching stored topic under its existing key.
    - Rule 7 then makes a new unit only when the previous one is terminal.
    - Deleting the sqlite adapter deletes this supplier with it, so the delete test still passes.
15. **`H.ops.memory.read(...journals)`.** This comes from scenario 4, where a journal of operational experience is read by the operator and by no prompt.
    - `write` and `curate` both grant more than reading, so neither is the honest grant for a read-only client.
    - Reading memory is an operation like any other, granted per journal.

  export interface FlowShape<I, A, E extends string, X> extends K.EntityRef<'flow'> {
    readonly __flow?: {
      readonly input: (input: I) => void;
      readonly steps: A;
      readonly exits: E;
      readonly scope: (scope: X) => void;
    };
  }

  export interface ExitedFlow<I, A, E extends string, X = {}> extends FlowShape<I, A, E, X> {
    readonly exited: true;
  }

  export type StepsOf<F> = F extends FlowShape<infer _I, infer A, infer _E, infer _X> ? A : never;

  export interface Flow<I, A, E extends string, X = {}> extends FlowShape<I, A, E, X> {
    input<S extends z.ZodType>(schema: S): Flow<z.output<S>, A, E, X>;
    resources(select: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => ReadonlyArray<Resource | Lease>): Flow<I, A, E, X>;
    facet(facet: Facet, value: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => string): Flow<I, A, E, X>;
    step<N extends string, SI, O>(
      name: N,
      executable: Executable<SI, O>,
      map: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => NoInfer<SI>,
      options?: StepOptions<FlowState<I, A, X>>,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: O }, E, X>;
    step<N extends string, O>(
      name: N,
      executable: Executable<void, O>,
      options?: StepOptions<FlowState<I, A, X>>,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: O }, E, X>;
    step<N extends string, O>(
      name: N,
      executable: Executable<I, O>,
      options?: StepOptions<FlowState<I, A, X>>,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: O }, E, X>;
    when<A2, E2 extends string = never>(
      predicate: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => boolean,
      branch: (flow: Flow<I, A, never, X>) => FlowShape<I, A2, E2, X>,
    ): Flow<I, A & Partial<Omit<A2, keyof A>>, E | E2, X>;
    parallel<
      N extends string,
      B extends { readonly [branch: string]: (flow: Flow<I, A, never, X>) => FlowShape<I, object, never, X> },
    >(
      name: N,
      branches: B,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: { readonly [Q in keyof B]: Omit<StepsOf<ReturnType<B[Q]>>, keyof A> } }, E, X>;
    loop<N extends string, C, A2, E2 extends string = never>(
      name: N,
      spec: {
        readonly maxIterations: number | ((state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => number);
        readonly initial: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => C;
        readonly body: (flow: Flow<I, A, never, X & LoopScope<C>>) => FlowShape<I, A2, E2, X & LoopScope<C>>;
        readonly next: (state: FlowState<I, A2, X & LoopScope<C>>) => C;
        readonly until: (state: FlowState<I, A2, X & LoopScope<C>>) => boolean;
      },
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: LoopResult<C> }, E | E2, X>;
    halt<N extends string, C, D>(
      name: N,
      halt: Halt<C, D>,
      context: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => NoInfer<C>,
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: D }, E, X>;
    halt<N extends string, D>(name: N, halt: Halt<void, D>): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: D }, E, X>;
    spawn<N extends string, CD>(
      name: N,
      lane: LaneRef<CD>,
      items: (state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => readonly NoInfer<CD>[],
    ): Flow<I, A & { readonly [P in N]: readonly K.ChildResult[] }, E, X>;
    exit<L extends string>(label: L | ((state: FlowState<I, A, X>) => L)): ExitedFlow<I, A, E | L, X>;
  }

  export interface Supply<D> extends K.EntityRef<'supply'> {
    readonly __supplies?: D;
    map<D2>(map: (raw: D) => D2): Supply<D2>;
    key(key: (data: D) => string): Supply<D>;
    updatesOnly(): Update<D>;
  }

  export interface Update<D> extends K.EntityRef<'supply'> {
    readonly __updates?: D;
  }

  export interface ExitBound<St extends State> {
    readonly to: St;
    readonly maxTimes: number;
    readonly then: St;
  }

  export interface Arcs<St extends State, E extends string> {
    readonly exits: { readonly [L in E]: St | ExitBound<St> };
    readonly retry: K.Retry & { readonly exhausted: St };
  }

  export interface LaneRef<D> extends K.EntityRef<'lane'> {
    readonly __accepts?: (data: D) => void;
  }

  export interface Lane<D, St extends State> extends LaneRef<D> {
    readonly __states?: St;
    from(...suppliers: ReadonlyArray<Supply<D> | Update<Partial<D>>>): Lane<D, St>;
    store(store: K.Store): Lane<D, St>;
    handle<E extends string>(flow: ExitedFlow<D, object, E>, arcs: Arcs<St, NoInfer<E>>): Lane<D, St>;
    handle<I, E extends string>(
      flow: ExitedFlow<I, object, E>,
      arcs: Arcs<St, NoInfer<E>> & { readonly input: (unit: K.UnitView<D>) => NoInfer<I> },

    ceiling(ceiling: {

      readonly onExceed: Halt<K.CeilingContext, K.CeilingDecision> | 'fail';
    }): Lane<D, St>;
    after(predecessor: (data: D) => string | undefined, options: { readonly failed: St }): Lane<D, St>;
    facet(facet: Facet, value: (data: D) => string): Lane<D, St>;
    deadline(deadline: (unit: K.UnitView<D>) => Date | undefined): Lane<D, St>;
  }

  export interface LaneStart {
    of<D, St extends State>(kind: WorkKind<D, St>): Lane<D, St>;
  }

  export interface Journal<C> extends K.JournalRef<C> {

  }

  export interface JournalStart {
    of<C>(kind: MemoryKind<C>): Journal<C>;
  }

  export interface Trigger<P> extends K.EntityRef<'trigger'> {
    when(predicate: (payload: P) => boolean): Trigger<P>;
    do(...consequences: ReadonlyArray<Consequence<P>>): Trigger<P>;
  }

    on<P>(source: Source<P>): Trigger<P>;
  }

  export interface Operation extends K.EntityRef<'operation'> {}

  export interface Grant extends K.EntityRef<'grant'> {
    readonly client: K.Client;

  }

  export interface Harness extends K.EntityRef<'harness'> {
    ledger(ledger: K.Ledger): Harness;

  }

    flow(name: string): Flow<void, {}, never>;

    };

    trigger(name: string): TriggerStart;
    entered<D, St extends State>(lane: Lane<D, St>, ...states: readonly NoInfer<St>[]): Source<K.Entered<D>>;
    streak<D, St extends State>(

    run<I, P>(command: Command<I, unknown>, map: (payload: P) => NoInfer<I>): Consequence<P>;
    resolve<C, D>(halt: Halt<C, D>, decide: (payload: K.HaltOpened<C>) => NoInfer<D>): Consequence<K.HaltOpened<C>>;

      seat(name: string, decide: (input: K.SeatPolicyInput) => readonly K.ModelRef[]): SeatPolicy;

      recall(name: string, decide: (input: K.RecallInput) => readonly K.RecallCandidate[]): RecallPolicy;
      halt<C, D>(

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { Candidate } from 'harness-dsl/kernel';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { linear } from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import { supply } from 'harness-dsl/supply';
import { policies } from 'harness-dsl/policies';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';
import { plugins } from 'harness-dsl/plugins';

const todo = H.state('todo').pending();
const inProgress = H.state('inProgress').active();
const needsReview = H.state('needsReview').waiting();
const done = H.state('done').terminal('success');
const wontDo = H.state('wontDo').terminal('neutral');
const abandoned = H.state('abandoned').terminal('failure');

const scheduled = H.state('scheduled').pending();
const probing = H.state('probing').active();
const healthy = H.state('healthy').terminal('success');
const unhealthy = H.state('unhealthy').terminal('failure');

const taskSchema = z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string(), ref: z.string() });
const featureSchema = taskSchema.extend({ epicRef: z.string().optional() });
const deliverySchema = taskSchema.extend({ rounds: z.number().int().positive() });
const heartbeatSchema = z.object({ service: z.string() });

const Epic = H.work('Epic').schema(taskSchema).states(todo, inProgress, needsReview, done, wontDo, abandoned);
const Feature = H.work('Feature').schema(featureSchema).states(todo, inProgress, needsReview, done, wontDo, abandoned);
const Bug = H.work('Bug').schema(taskSchema).states(todo, inProgress, needsReview, done, wontDo, abandoned);
const ServiceHeartbeat = H.work('ServiceHeartbeat').schema(heartbeatSchema).states(scheduled, probing, healthy, unhealthy);

const experience = H.memory('experience').content(z.object({ lesson: z.string() })).trust('experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste').content(z.object({ preference: z.string() })).trust('taste');

const experienceJournal = H.journal('experience')
  .of(experience)
  .store(jsonl.store('memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 8 }));
const tasteJournal = H.journal('taste')
  .of(taste)
  .store(jsonl.store('memory/taste.jsonl'))
  .recall(policies.specificity({ limit: 12 }));

const payments = H.resource('payments');
const webApp = H.resource('webApp');
const platform = H.resource('platform');

const projectChecks = H.command('projectChecks').run(async (_, ctx) => {
  const result = await ctx.sh('npm run check');
  if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(`${result.stdout}\n${result.stderr}`);
});

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .prompt('You implement one unit of work in this repository and leave it passing its checks.')
  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience, taste)
  .use(
    plugins.gitWorktreeIsolation(),
    plugins.fileLeaseGuard([
      { resource: payments, globs: ['src/payments/**', 'migrations/**'] },
      { resource: webApp, globs: ['src/web/**'] },
      { resource: platform, globs: ['src/platform/**', 'package.json'] },
    ]),
    plugins.stopCheck(projectChecks),
  );

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .prompt('You audit a change against its task and list every deficit that remains.')
  .intents(['read', 'shell'])
  .recall(experience)
  .record(experience)
  .use(plugins.gitWorktreeIsolation());

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .prompt('You decompose an epic into independently shippable features.')
  .intents(['read'])
  .recall(taste);

const buildSkill = H.skill('build')
  .input(z.object({ task: z.string(), deficits: z.array(z.string()), guidance: z.string().optional() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), needsDecision: z.boolean(), question: z.string().optional() }))
  .prompt(i => `Task:\n${i.task}\n\nOpen deficits:\n${i.deficits.join('\n') || 'none'}\n\nOwner guidance: ${i.guidance ?? 'none'}`);

const auditSkill = H.skill('audit')
  .input(z.object({ task: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(i => `Task:\n${i.task}\n\nBuilder summary:\n${i.summary}\n\nList the deficits that remain.`);

const planSkill = H.skill('plan')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt(i => `Epic: ${i.title}\n\n${i.body}`);

const sharedQuota = sqlite.quota('~/.harness/quota.db');
const subscriptionA = H.account('subscription-a', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_A') })).maxQuotaShare(0.8).quota(sharedQuota);
const subscriptionB = H.account('subscription-b', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_B') })).maxQuotaShare(0.6).quota(sharedQuota);
const subscriptionC = H.account('subscription-c', claudeCode.driver({ configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_C') })).maxQuotaShare(0.5).quota(sharedQuota);
const apiAccount = H.account('api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }));

const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5', { effort: 'medium' }).pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const opus = H.model('claude-opus-4-1', { effort: 'high' }).pricing(anthropic.pricing());

const claudePool = H.pool('claude', [subscriptionA, subscriptionB, subscriptionC])
  .serves(sonnet, opus)
  .policy(policies.soonestExpiring())
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const unitSuccess = H.metric('unitSuccess').rate(H.events.terminal({ verdict: 'success' }), H.events.terminal());

const cheaperUntilWorse = H.policy.seat('cheaperUntilWorse', ({ seat, unit, metrics }) => {
  const cheap = metrics.read(unitSuccess, { window: '14d', where: { kind: unit.kind, seat, model: sonnet } });
  const cheapFalls = cheap.samples >= 20 && cheap.value !== undefined && cheap.value < 0.85;
  return cheapFalls ? [opus, sonnet] : [sonnet, opus];
});

const builder = H.seat('builder').role(builderRole).models(sonnet, opus).policy(cheaperUntilWorse);
const auditor = H.seat('auditor').role(auditorRole).models(opus);
const planner = H.seat('planner').role(plannerRole).models(opus);

const ownerDecision = H.halt('ownerDecision')
  .context(z.object({ task: z.string(), question: z.string() }))
  .ask(c => `${c.task}: ${c.question}`)
  .decision(z.object({ answer: z.string() }));

interface Rounds {
  readonly deficits: string[];
  readonly guidance: string | undefined;
}

const delivery = H.flow('delivery')
  .input(deliverySchema)
  .loop('rounds', {
    maxIterations: s => s.input.rounds,
    initial: (): Rounds => ({ deficits: [], guidance: undefined }),
    body: f =>
      f
        .step('build', builder.call(buildSkill), s => ({
          task: `${s.input.title}\n\n${s.input.body}`,
          deficits: s.carry.deficits,
          guidance: s.carry.guidance,
        }))
        .when(
          s => s.steps.build.needsDecision,
          b => b.halt('ownerDecision', ownerDecision, s => ({ task: s.input.title, question: s.steps.build.question ?? s.steps.build.summary })),
        )
        .step('audit', auditor.call(auditSkill), s => ({ task: s.input.body, summary: s.steps.build.summary })),
    next: s => ({ deficits: s.steps.audit.deficits, guidance: s.steps.ownerDecision?.answer }),
    until: s => s.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0,
  })
  .exit(s => (s.steps.rounds.completed ? 'delivered' : 'deficitsRemain'));

const linearKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const tracker = linear.store({
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'ENG',
  statuses: [
    [todo, 'Todo'],
    [inProgress, 'In Progress'],
    [needsReview, 'In Review'],
    [done, 'Done'],
    [wontDo, 'Canceled'],
    [abandoned, 'Abandoned'],
  ],
});

const bugs = H.lane('bugs')
  .of(Bug)
  .from(
    linear.issues({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'ENG', labels: ['bug'] })
      .map(issue => ({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, ref: issue.identifier }))
      .key(bug => bug.ref),
    supply.folder({ path: 'inbox/bugs', schema: z.object({ slug: z.string(), title: z.string(), body: z.string() }) })
      .map(file => ({ title: file.title, body: file.body, ref: `file:${file.slug}` }))
      .key(bug => bug.ref),
    supply.manual(),
  )
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(delivery, {
    exits: { delivered: done, deficitsRemain: needsReview },
    retry: { tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: abandoned },
    input: unit => ({ title: unit.data.title, body: unit.data.body, ref: unit.data.ref, rounds: 3 }),
  })
  .wip(2);

const features = H.lane('features')
  .of(Feature)
  .from(
    linear.issues({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'ENG', labels: ['feature'] })
      .map(issue => ({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, ref: issue.identifier, epicRef: issue.parentId }))
      .key(feature => feature.ref),
    supply.manual(),
  )
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(delivery, {
    exits: { delivered: done, deficitsRemain: needsReview },
    retry: { tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: abandoned },
    input: unit => ({ title: unit.data.title, body: unit.data.body, ref: unit.data.ref, rounds: 5 }),
  });

const decompose = H.flow('decompose')
  .input(taskSchema)
  .step('plan', planner.call(planSkill), s => ({ title: s.input.title, body: s.input.body }))
  .spawn('features', features, s =>
    s.steps.plan.features.map((feature, index) => ({
      title: feature.title,
      body: feature.body,
      ref: `${s.input.ref}/${index + 1}`,
      epicRef: s.input.ref,
    })),
  )
  .exit(s => (s.steps.features.every(child => child.verdict === 'success') ? 'delivered' : 'featuresUnfinished'));

const epics = H.lane('epics')
  .of(Epic)
  .from(
    linear.issues({ apiKey: linearKey, team: 'ENG', labels: ['epic'] })
      .map(issue => ({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, ref: issue.identifier }))
      .key(epic => epic.ref),
  )
  .store(tracker)
  .handle(decompose, {
    exits: { delivered: done, featuresUnfinished: needsReview },
    retry: { tries: 1, backoff: 'none', exhausted: abandoned },
  })
  .wip(1);

const probeService = H.command('probeService')
  .input(heartbeatSchema)
  .output(z.object({ healthy: z.boolean(), detail: z.string() }))
  .run(async (input, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(`curl -fsS --max-time 10 https://${input.service}.internal/healthz`);
    return { healthy: result.code === 0, detail: result.code === 0 ? result.stdout : result.stderr };
  });

const heartbeat = H.flow('heartbeat')
  .input(heartbeatSchema)
  .step('probe', probeService)
  .exit(s => (s.steps.probe.healthy ? 'healthy' : 'unhealthy'));

const heartbeats = H.lane('heartbeats')
  .of(ServiceHeartbeat)
  .from(
    supply.schedule({ cron: '*/5 * * * *', units: () => [{ service: 'api' }, { service: 'web' }, { service: 'worker' }] })
      .key(beat => beat.service),
  )
  .handle(heartbeat, {
    exits: { healthy, unhealthy },
    retry: { tries: 0, backoff: 'none', exhausted: unhealthy },
  });

const heartbeatFailureFilesBug = H.trigger('heartbeatFailureFilesBug')
  .on(H.entered(heartbeats, unhealthy))
  .do(
    H.create(
      bugs,
      p => ({
        title: `${p.unit.data.service} heartbeat failed`,
        body: `The five-minute heartbeat for ${p.unit.data.service} failed at ${p.unit.updatedAt.toISOString()}.`,
        ref: `heartbeat:${p.unit.data.service}`,
      }),
      { key: p => `heartbeat:${p.unit.data.service}` },
    ),
  );

const featureStarvationSeconds = 4 * 3600;

const lanePriority = (candidate: Candidate): number => {
  if (candidate.lane === heartbeats) return 0;
  if (candidate.lane === features && candidate.waitingSeconds > featureStarvationSeconds) return 1;
  if (candidate.lane === bugs) return 2;
  if (candidate.lane === features) return 3;
  return 4;
};

const teamOrder = H.policy.schedule('teamOrder', ({ candidates }) =>
  [...candidates].sort((a, b) => lanePriority(a) - lanePriority(b) || b.waitingSeconds - a.waitingSeconds),
);

const probeProduction = H.command('probeProduction')
  .output(z.object({ healthy: z.boolean(), detail: z.string() }))
  .run(async (_, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh('curl -fsS --max-time 10 https://app.example.com/healthz');
    return { healthy: result.code === 0, detail: result.code === 0 ? result.stdout : result.stderr };
  });

const supervisor = claudeCode.client('supervisor');

const supervisorGrant = H.grant(
  supervisor,
  H.ops.work.read,
  H.ops.work.write,
  H.ops.resolve(ownerDecision),
  H.ops.memory.write(experienceJournal, tasteJournal),
  H.ops.telemetry.read,
  H.ops.accounts.manage,
  H.operation('productionHealth', probeProduction),
);

export default H.harness('coding-team')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .pools(claudePool)
  .lanes(heartbeats, bugs, features, epics)
  .journals(experienceJournal, tasteJournal)
  .triggers(heartbeatFailureFilesBug)
  .schedule(teamOrder)
  .grants(supervisorGrant)
  .metrics(unitSuccess)
  .observe(observers.board({ path: 'BOARD.md' }), observers.telemetry({ path: 'TELEMETRY.md' }));

=== END ===

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { http } from 'harness-dsl/http';
import { supply } from 'harness-dsl/supply';
import { observers } from 'harness-dsl/observers';

const local = H.runner.local('worker', { slots: 4 });
const unitStore = sqlite.store('.harness/units.db');

const apiAccount = H.account('anthropic-api', anthropic.api({ apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }));
const sonnet = H.model('claude-sonnet-4-5').pricing(anthropic.pricing());
const pool = H.pool('api', [apiAccount]).serves(sonnet);

const proposed = H.state('proposed').pending();
const observing = H.state('observing').active();
const aWins = H.state('a-wins').terminal('success');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins').terminal('success');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive').terminal('neutral');
const abandoned = H.state('abandoned').terminal('failure');

const experimentSchema = z.object({ experimentId: z.string(), variantA: z.string(), variantB: z.string(), metric: z.string() });
const experiment = H.work('experiment').schema(experimentSchema).states(proposed, observing, aWins, bWins, inconclusive, abandoned);

const winnerOf = (text: string): 'a' | 'b' | 'none' => {
  const winner = text.trim();
  return winner === 'a' || winner === 'b' ? winner : 'none';
};

const twoWeekObservation = H.job('two-week-observation')
  .input(experimentSchema)
  .output(z.object({ winner: z.enum(['a', 'b', 'none']) }))
  .submit(async (i, ctx) => {
    const started = await ctx.sh(`experiments start ${i.experimentId} --a ${i.variantA} --b ${i.variantB} --days 14`);
    if (started.code !== 0) throw new Error(started.stderr);
    return i.experimentId;
  })
  .collect(async (ref, ctx) => {
    const sample = await ctx.sh(`experiments sample ${ref}`);
    if (sample.code !== 0) return { status: 'failed', reason: sample.stderr };
    const verdict = await ctx.sh(`experiments verdict ${ref}`);
    if (verdict.stdout.trim() === 'running') return { status: 'running' };
    return { status: 'done', output: { winner: winnerOf(verdict.stdout) } };
  })
  .poll('1h');

const runExperiment = H.flow('run-experiment')
  .input(experimentSchema)
  .step('observation', twoWeekObservation)
  .exit(s =>
    s.steps.observation.winner === 'a' ? 'a-wins' : s.steps.observation.winner === 'b' ? 'b-wins' : 'inconclusive',
  );

const experiments = H.lane('experiments')
  .of(experiment)
  .from(supply.manual(experimentSchema))
  .store(unitStore)
  .handle(runExperiment, {
    exits: { 'a-wins': aWins, 'b-wins': bWins, inconclusive },
    retry: { tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 600, exhausted: abandoned },
  });

const reviewDue = H.state('review-due').pending();
const reviewing = H.state('reviewing').active();
const customer = H.state('customer').waiting();
const suspended = H.state('suspended').waiting();
const reviewStalled = H.state('review-stalled').waiting();
const churned = H.state('churned').terminal('neutral');

const tenancySchema = z.object({ tenantId: z.string(), plan: z.string() });
const tenancy = H.work('tenancy').schema(tenancySchema).states(reviewDue, reviewing, customer, suspended, reviewStalled, churned);

const usageReview = H.command('usage-review')
  .input(tenancySchema)
  .output(z.object({ seats: z.number(), monthlyUsd: z.number(), trend: z.string() }))
  .runner(local)
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(`billing usage ${i.tenantId} --json`);
    const usage = z.object({ seats: z.number(), monthlyUsd: z.number(), trend: z.string() }).parse(JSON.parse(result.stdout));
    return usage;
  });

const offerUpsell = H.command('offer-upsell')
  .input(z.object({ tenantId: z.string(), note: z.string() }))
  .runner(local)
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const result = await ctx.sh(`crm upsell ${i.tenantId}`, { stdin: i.note });
    if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
  });

const summarizerRole = H.role('account-summarizer').prompt('Summarize a tenancy month for an account manager.');
const summarizeUsage = H.skill('summarize-usage')
  .input(z.object({ tenantId: z.string(), plan: z.string(), seats: z.number(), monthlyUsd: z.number(), trend: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ text: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Tenant ${i.tenantId} on ${i.plan}: ${i.seats} seats, $${i.monthlyUsd}/month, trend ${i.trend}.`);
const summarizer = H.seat('account-summarizer').role(summarizerRole).models(sonnet);

const upsell = H.halt('upsell')
  .context(z.object({ tenantId: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .ask(c => `Offer ${c.tenantId} an upsell?\n${c.summary}`)
  .decision(z.object({ upsell: z.boolean(), note: z.string() }));

const monthlyReview = H.flow('monthly-review')
  .input(tenancySchema)
  .step('usage', usageReview)
  .step('summary', summarizer.call(summarizeUsage), s => ({ ...s.input, ...s.steps.usage }))
  .halt('decision', upsell, s => ({ tenantId: s.input.tenantId, summary: s.steps.summary.text }))
  .when(
    s => s.steps.decision.upsell,
    f => f.step('offer', offerUpsell, s => ({ tenantId: s.input.tenantId, note: s.steps.decision.note })),
  )
  .exit('reviewed');

const tenancies = H.lane('tenancies')
  .of(tenancy)
  .from(supply.manual(tenancySchema))
  .store(unitStore)
  .deadline(unit =>
    unit.state === customer.name ? new Date(unit.updatedAt.getFullYear(), unit.updatedAt.getMonth() + 1, 1) : undefined,
  )
  .handle(monthlyReview, {
    exits: { reviewed: customer },
    retry: { tries: 3, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 3600, exhausted: reviewStalled },
  });

const roundDue = H.state('round-due').pending();
const drafting = H.state('drafting').active();
const awaitingVendor = H.state('awaiting-vendor').waiting();
const negotiationStalled = H.state('negotiation-stalled').waiting();
const agreed = H.state('agreed').terminal('success');
const weWalked = H.state('walked-away-by-us').terminal('neutral');
const theyWalked = H.state('walked-away-by-them').terminal('neutral');
const expired = H.state('expired').terminal('neutral');

const negotiationSchema = z.object({
  negotiationId: z.string(),
  vendor: z.string(),
  item: z.string(),
  ceilingUsd: z.number(),
  expiresAt: z.string(),
  lastVendorOffer: z.string().optional(),
  vendorWalkedAway: z.boolean().optional(),
});
const negotiation = H.work('negotiation')
  .schema(negotiationSchema)
  .states(roundDue, drafting, awaitingVendor, negotiationStalled, agreed, weWalked, theyWalked, expired);

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator').prompt('Draft the next procurement offer within the ceiling.');
const draftOffer = H.skill('draft-offer')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), ceilingUsd: z.number(), lastVendorOffer: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ action: z.enum(['offer', 'accept', 'walk-away']), message: z.string() }))
  .prompt(i => `Vendor ${i.vendor}, item ${i.item}, ceiling $${i.ceilingUsd}. Their last offer: ${i.lastVendorOffer}`);
const negotiator = H.seat('negotiator').role(negotiatorRole).models(sonnet);

const vendorUrl = H.env('PROCUREMENT_API_URL');
const sendToVendor = H.command('send-to-vendor')
  .input(z.object({ negotiationId: z.string(), action: z.enum(['offer', 'accept', 'walk-away']), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ messageId: z.string() }))
  .runner(local)
  .effect('unrepeatable')
  .detect(async (i, ctx) => {
    const response = await fetch(`${ctx.resolve(vendorUrl)}/negotiations/${i.negotiationId}/messages?attempt=${ctx.attempt.id}`);
    const sent = z.object({ messageId: z.string().optional() }).parse(await response.json());
    return sent.messageId === undefined ? undefined : { messageId: sent.messageId };
  })
  .run(async (i, ctx) => {
    const response = await fetch(`${ctx.resolve(vendorUrl)}/negotiations/${i.negotiationId}/messages`, {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ action: i.action, message: i.message, attempt: ctx.attempt.id }),
    });
    return z.object({ messageId: z.string() }).parse(await response.json());
  });

const negotiationRound = H.flow('negotiation-round')
  .input(negotiationSchema)
  .when(s => s.input.vendorWalkedAway === true, f => f.exit('they-walked'))
  .step('draft', negotiator.call(draftOffer), s => ({
    vendor: s.input.vendor,
    item: s.input.item,
    ceilingUsd: s.input.ceilingUsd,
    lastVendorOffer: s.input.lastVendorOffer ?? 'none yet',
  }))
  .step('send', sendToVendor, s => ({ negotiationId: s.input.negotiationId, action: s.steps.draft.action, message: s.steps.draft.message }))
  .exit(s => (s.steps.draft.action === 'accept' ? 'agreed' : s.steps.draft.action === 'walk-away' ? 'we-walked' : 'offered'));

const vendorReplies = http
  .webhook({
    path: '/procurement/replies',
    schema: z.object({ negotiationId: z.string(), lastVendorOffer: z.string(), vendorWalkedAway: z.boolean() }),
    secret: H.env('PROCUREMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
  })
  .key(reply => reply.negotiationId)
  .updatesOnly();

const negotiations = H.lane('negotiations')
  .of(negotiation)
  .from(supply.manual(negotiationSchema).key(d => d.negotiationId), vendorReplies)
  .store(unitStore)
  .deadline(unit => (unit.position === 'terminal' ? undefined : new Date(unit.data.expiresAt)))
  .handle(negotiationRound, {
    exits: { 'they-walked': theyWalked, agreed, 'we-walked': weWalked, offered: awaitingVendor },
    retry: { tries: 2, backoff: 'exponential', delaySeconds: 300, exhausted: negotiationStalled },
  });

const monthlyReviewDue = H.trigger('monthly-review-due').on(H.due(tenancies)).do(H.move(tenancies, reviewDue));
const negotiationExpiry = H.trigger('negotiation-expiry').on(H.due(negotiations)).do(H.move(negotiations, expired));

const inconclusiveRate = H.metric('experiments-inconclusive-rate').rate(
  H.events.entered(inconclusive),
  H.events.entered(aWins, bWins, inconclusive),
);
const churnCount = H.metric('tenancies-churned').count(H.events.entered(churned));
const agreementRate = H.metric('negotiations-agreed-rate').rate(
  H.events.entered(agreed),
  H.events.entered(agreed, weWalked, theyWalked, expired),
);

const roundsBeforeExperiments = H.policy.schedule('rounds-reviews-experiments', ({ candidates, metrics }) => {
  const reading = metrics.read(inconclusiveRate, { window: '180d', where: { kind: experiment } });
  const experimentsLast = reading.samples >= 10 && (reading.value ?? 0) > 0.5;
  const rounds = candidates.filter(c => c.lane === negotiations);
  const reviews = candidates.filter(c => c.lane === tenancies);
  const tests = candidates.filter(c => c.lane === experiments);
  return experimentsLast ? [...rounds, ...reviews, ...tests] : [...rounds, ...tests, ...reviews];
});

export default H.harness('hostile-lifecycles')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .pools(pool)
  .lanes(experiments, tenancies, negotiations)
  .triggers(monthlyReviewDue, negotiationExpiry)
  .schedule(roundsBeforeExperiments)
  .grants(
    H.grant(
      http.client('account-desk', { port: 8080, token: H.env('ACCOUNT_DESK_TOKEN') }),
      H.ops.work.read,
      H.ops.work.write,
      H.ops.resolve(upsell),
      H.ops.telemetry.read,
    ),
  )
  .metrics(inconclusiveRate, churnCount, agreementRate)
  .observe(observers.board({ path: '.harness/board.md' }));

=== END ===

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface. A step is a command, a model call, a batch of model calls, or an external job (submitted now, collected later by a poll or a callback: a cloud batch, a GPU run, a long service call); a batch and an external job hold no capacity while they run. (External jobs ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role, resource, halt). A resource (a file pattern, a database, a section, a host) is a named shared thing that leases, memory scope and metric facets reference by identity; a string never stands in for it. A halt is a named question with a decision schema that grants, metrics, timers and policies reference by identity. *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall, seat = role × models × choice policy: a seat holds a role with the model a deterministic policy picks at attempt time, an agent is a seat with one model, and metrics on an A/B comparison key on the seat so a model swap does not break the series). (Resources, halts and seats ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts. By default a failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy, and the lane's policy names where exhaustion leaves the unit, in the kind's own states; the kind declares nothing about failure. Where an active unit stands in its work is its attempt's current step, read from the ledger; a kind declares no states for it, and waiting on a human is the attempt's blocked state, recorded once. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why. The failure default was added after generation 1, when three of eleven children read the silence as "every kind declares a failure state" and invented states that loop or dead-end. Retry's end state moved to the lane, and the active position was ruled, on 2026-11-01 after run one: three generation-3 adversaries showed a move on the kind only means something given the lane's policy, and three generations modelled waiting on a human twice.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable, and it may be partitioned by backend. Account quota shared by several harnesses is a ledger partition of append-only quota events: each harness appends its own consumption and folds the window at read time, so no harness takes a lock over another's account state. The account names its quota partition, as every instance carries its backend; the ledger carries no option for it. A quota store that needs the ledger's single-writer lock, or a second store under the ledger's name, breaks this principle. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all. (Shared quota ruled 2026-11-01 after generation 1.)
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted; a grant names the halt it may resolve. A halt's resolver is a human, a registered policy (a deterministic function whose decision is recorded with the metrics and sample counts it read), or a clock: a timeout default that resolves the halt without cancelling the attempt. Deadlines on a halt run from the recorded halt, never from unit data. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished". A metric dimension is a typed ledger column (kind, lane, state, model, seat, resource, halt) or a declared facet entity; a facet that repeats a column is a startup error. (Ruled 2026-11-01 after run one.)

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.
